title.zh: 卷256 列傳四十三 蔡毓荣 哈占 董卫国 周有德 伊闢
title.en: Volume 256 Biographies 43: Cai Yurong, Ha Zhan, Dong Weiguo, Zhou Youde, Yi Pi
title.raw: 卷256 列傳四十三 蔡毓荣 哈占 董卫国 周有德 伊闢

sentences.zh: 蔡毓榮，字仁庵，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Cai Yurong, styled Ren'an, was a member of the Hanjun Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yurong, styled Ren'an, belonged to the Hanjun Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父士英，初籍錦州。

translations.literal: His father was Shiying, who was originally registered at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shiying was originally domiciled in Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 從祖大壽來降，授世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: He followed his kinsman Dashou in coming over to surrender and was granted the hereditary office of niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his kinsman Zu Dashou in submitting to the Qing and was granted the hereditary rank of company captain.

sentences.zh: 從轉戰有功。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigns and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in successive campaigns.

sentences.zh: 順治間，累遷至右副都御使。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi reign he was promoted in successive steps to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi he rose through successive appointments to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 出為江西巡撫，疏陳兵後荒蕪，請除荒田賦額十萬八千五百四十頃有奇；

translations.literal: He went out as Jiangxi provincial governor and in a memorial described post-war desolation, requesting removal of tax quotas on wasteland amounting to more than 108,540 qing;
translations.idiomatic: Appointed governor of Jiangxi, he memorialized on the devastation left by the wars and asked that tax quotas on more than 108,540 qing of abandoned fields be cancelled;

sentences.zh: 又以瑞、袁二府科糧偏重，疏請蠲瑞屬浮糧九萬九千餘石，定袁屬賦額自一斗六升七八合減至九升三合：皆得請。

translations.literal: He also stated that the grain levies in the two prefectures of Rui and Yuan were excessively heavy, and in a memorial requested exemption of more than 99,000 shi of surplus grain in Rui jurisdiction and fixing Yuan jurisdiction assessments from one dou six sheng seven-eight he down to nine sheng three he: all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that grain quotas in Rui and Yuan prefectures were unduly heavy, sought remission of more than 99,000 shi of excess levies in Rui, and had Yuan assessments cut from about 1.67 dou per mu to 0.93 dou; all these requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 又疏論銅塘封禁山不宜開採，咸為民所頌。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that the sealed Tongtang mountain should not be opened for mining, and all these measures were praised by the people.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued that the sealed Tongtang hills should not be mined, measures the people widely praised.

sentences.zh: 尋改漕運總督，加兵部尚書，以疾告歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Canal transport governor, given the additional title Minister of War, and retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Canal transport governor with the concurrent rank of Minister of War, then retired owing to illness.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，諡襄敏。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died and was given the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the reign he died and was posthumously titled Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 毓榮，其次子也。

translations.literal: Yurong was his second son.
translations.idiomatic: Yurong was Shiying's second son.

sentences.zh: 初授佐領，兼刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He was first appointed assistant commandant and concurrently served as a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made an assistant banner captain while also serving as a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尋授御史，兼參領，遷秘書院學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made censor, concurrently served as deputy banner commander, and was transferred to academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed censor and deputy banner commander, then promoted to Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，授侍郎，歷刑、吏二部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangxi reign he was appointed vice minister and served in succession in the Ministries of Punishments and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi he became a vice minister and served in turn in the Ministries of Punishments and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，授四川湖廣總督，駐荊州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan and Huguang, stationed at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made governor-general of Sichuan and Huguang with his headquarters at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 累疏言：「四川民少田荒，請廣招開墾。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized, saying: "Sichuan has few people and much wasteland; please widely recruit settlers to open and cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized: "Sichuan has too few people and too much fallow land; we should recruit settlers on a broad scale.

sentences.zh: 招民三百戶，予議敘​​，墾田五年，起科」；

translations.literal: For recruiting three hundred households, grant consideration for promotion; after five years of cultivation, begin taxation";
translations.idiomatic: Recruit three hundred households and grant merit consideration; after five years of cultivation, begin taxation";

sentences.zh: 「四川衝要營員用沿邊例題補」；

translations.literal: "Use the frontier precedent for filling key garrison posts in Sichuan";
translations.idiomatic: "Fill key Sichuan garrison posts under the frontier appointment rules";

sentences.zh: 「移駐官兵子弟得入籍應試」。

translations.literal: "Children of relocated garrison troops may register domicile and sit for examinations."
translations.idiomatic: "Let children of relocated garrison troops register locally and take the civil examinations."

sentences.zh: 並下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All proposals were sent to the ministries for review and implementation.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吳三桂反，毓榮遣沅州總兵崔世祿率兵入貴州，夷陵總兵徐治都、永州總兵李芝蘭繼進，上命速遣提督桑額守沅州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled; Yurong sent Yuanzhou regional commander Cui Shilu to lead troops into Guizhou, with Yiling regional commander Xu Zhidu and Yongzhou regional commander Li Zhilan following in support, and the emperor ordered the prompt dispatch of Grand Coordinator Sang'e to defend Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rose in rebellion. Yurong sent Yuanzhou commander Cui Shilu into Guizhou, with Yiling commander Xu Zhidu and Yongzhou commander Li Zhilan advancing behind him; the emperor ordered Grand Coordinator Sang'e sent at once to hold Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋授順承郡王勒爾錦為大將軍，率八旗兵討三桂，駐荊州，諭毓榮督餉。

translations.literal: Soon Prince Shuncheng Le'erjin was appointed grand general, leading the Eight Banners to suppress Sangui, stationed at Jingzhou, and Yurong was instructed to supervise supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuncheng Le'erjin was soon appointed grand general to lead the Eight Banners against Sangui from Jingzhou, with orders that Yurong supervise provisions.

sentences.zh: 十三年，分設四川總督，命毓榮專督湖廣，以招民墾荒功，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year a separate Sichuan governor-general was established and Yurong was ordered to supervise Huguang exclusively; for his merit in recruiting settlers to reclaim wasteland he was given the additional title Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Sichuan received its own governor-general while Yurong was left in charge of Huguang alone; for recruiting settlers to open wasteland he was given the concurrent rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三桂破沅州，世祿降。

translations.literal: Sangui captured Yuanzhou and Shilu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui took Yuanzhou and Shilu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 常德、澧州、長沙、岳州相繼陷。

translations.literal: Changde, Lizhou, Changsha, and Yuezhou fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Changde, Lizhou, Changsha, and Yuezhou then fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 部議毓​​榮當奪官，命留任。

translations.literal: The ministries deliberated that Yurong should be stripped of office, but he was ordered to remain in his post.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries recommended stripping Yurong of office, but the throne ordered him to remain in post.

sentences.zh: 尋居父喪，命在任守制，督綠旗兵進剿。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his father and was ordered to observe mourning in office while directing Green Standard troops in advance and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his father but was ordered to observe filial rites without leaving office while leading Green Standard forces against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 毓榮令副將胡士英等分防江口。

translations.literal: Yurong ordered Deputy Generals Hu Shiying and others to divide defense of the river mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Yurong had Deputy Generals Hu Shiying and others divide the defense of the river mouths.

sentences.zh: 叛將楊來嘉據南漳，屢出掠，令襄陽總兵劉成龍御之，戰屢勝。

translations.literal: The rebel general Yang Laijia held Nanzhang and repeatedly raided; Yurong ordered Xiangyang regional commander Liu Chenglong to resist him, and in battle repeatedly won.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Yang Laijia held Nanzhang and raided repeatedly; Yurong sent Xiangyang commander Liu Chenglong against him, who won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 廣西提督馬雄降三桂，騰書兩廣總督金光祖，言毓榮將率綠營兵赴岳州降三桂。

translations.literal: Guangxi provincial military commissioner Ma Xiong surrendered to Sangui and sent a sealed letter to Guangdong-Guangxi governor-general Jin Guangzu, saying Yurong was about to lead Green Battalion troops to Yuezhou to surrender to Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi commander Ma Xiong defected to Sangui and wrote secretly to Guangdong-Guangxi governor Jin Guangzu claiming Yurong would lead his Green troops to Yuezhou to join Sangui.

sentences.zh: 光祖密使告毓榮，毓榮以聞，請解任，命殫心供職，毋以反間引嫌。

translations.literal: Guangzu secretly sent word to Yurong; Yurong reported it and requested removal from office, but was ordered to devote himself wholeheartedly to duty and not let enemy disinformation raise suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu warned Yurong in secret; Yurong reported the matter and asked to be relieved, but was told to serve wholeheartedly and not let enemy disinformation sow doubt.

sentences.zh: 十四年，勒爾錦請增綠旗兵援、剿二營，領以兩副將，命毓榮統轄。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Le'erjin requested two additional Green Banner battalions for relief and suppression, each led by a deputy general, and Yurong was ordered to command them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Le'erjin asked for two more Green Banner battalions for relief and suppression, each under a deputy general, with Yurong placed in overall command.

sentences.zh: 十七年，毓榮督造戰艦成，率綠旗兵五千，從大將軍貝勒尚善進攻岳州，與討逆將軍鄂納等以舟八百餘入洞庭湖，擊三桂兵，大敗之，發砲沈其舟，殲寇甚眾。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Yurong supervised completion of warships, led five thousand Green Standard troops, and followed Grand General Prince Shangshan in attacking Yuezhou; with Pacification General E'na and others he entered Dongting Lake with more than eight hundred boats, struck Sangui's forces, routed them utterly, fired cannon and sank their vessels, and destroyed very many rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, after the warships he supervised were finished, Yurong led five thousand Green Standard troops with Grand General Prince Shangshan against Yuezhou. With Pacification General E'na he took more than eight hundred boats into Dongting Lake, crushed Sangui's fleet, sank many vessels by cannon fire, and killed rebels in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 遣將艤君山，載土伐木塞諸港。

translations.literal: He sent generals to moor at Junshan, load earth, cut timber, and block the various harbors.
translations.idiomatic: He sent officers to anchor at Junshan, haul earth, cut timber, and block the lake's channels.

sentences.zh: 分兵屯三眼橋、七里山，絕寇轉糧道。

translations.literal: He divided troops to garrison Sanyan Bridge and Qili Mountain, cutting off the rebels' supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were posted at Sanyan Bridge and Qili Mountain to sever the rebels' supply lines.

sentences.zh: 寇犯我糧艘，夾擊，復大敗之，斬級千餘。

translations.literal: When rebels attacked our grain convoy he attacked from both sides and again routed them, taking more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck the grain fleet he caught them in a pincer, routed them again, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 會三桂死，其孫世璠以喪還。

translations.literal: When Sangui died his grandson Shifan returned with the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui died, and his grandson Shifan withdrew with the funeral procession.

sentences.zh: 師克岳州，進定長沙、衡州。

translations.literal: The army captured Yuezhou and advanced to secure Changsha and Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The army took Yuezhou and went on to recover Changsha and Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，疏言：「湖南境惟辰州尚為三桂守。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he memorialized: "Within Hunan only Chenzhou is still held for Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he wrote: "Of Hunan, only Chenzhou still holds out for Sangui.

sentences.zh: 楓木嶺、神龍岡兩道皆險隘。

translations.literal: Both routes through Fengmu Ridge and Shenlong Ridge are precipitous and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Fengmu Ridge and Shenlong Ridge passes are steep and narrow.

sentences.zh: 我師疲頓，當小休。

translations.literal: Our army is exhausted and should rest briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are worn out and should pause briefly.

sentences.zh: 俟糧草克繼，會師進攻。」

translations.literal: Wait until grain and fodder can be supplied in succession, then unite the armies for the attack."
translations.idiomatic: Once supplies are steady again, the armies should advance together."

sentences.zh: 上命給事中摩羅、郎中伊爾格圖傳諭曰：「賊敗遁負險，宜用綠旗步兵。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Supervising Secretary Moluo and Director Yiergetu to transmit an edict, saying: "The rebels have been defeated and fled to hold the defiles; Green Standard infantry should be used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Supervising Secretary Moluo and Director Yiergetu with orders: "The rebels have fled to the defiles; use Green Standard infantry.

sentences.zh: 毓榮所屬官兵強壯，不難攻取險隘，剿除餘寇。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers under Yurong are strong and vigorous; it will not be difficult to seize the defiles and exterminate the remaining rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yurong's troops are strong; they should have little trouble taking the passes and wiping out the remnant rebels.

sentences.zh: 其具方略以聞。」

translations.literal: Let him set forth his plan and report."
translations.idiomatic: Have him submit a detailed plan."

sentences.zh: 毓榮疏請專責一人，總統諸路綠旗兵水陸並進，上即授毓榮綏遠將軍，賜敕，總統綠旗兵，總督董衛國、周有德、提督趙賴等並受節制。

translations.literal: Yurong memorialized requesting that one man be given sole responsibility to command all Green Standard forces on land and water in joint advance; the emperor at once appointed Yurong Pacification General, granted an imperial patent, placed all Green Standard troops under his command, and governors-general Dong Weiguo and Zhou Youde and provincial military commissioner Zhao Lai and others were all placed under his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Yurong asked that one commander take charge of all Green Standard forces advancing by land and water. The emperor immediately made him Pacification General with an imperial patent, put all Green troops under him, and placed governors Dong Weiguo and Zhou Youde and commander Zhao Lai under his orders.

sentences.zh: 十九年，督兵分道出楓木嶺、辰龍關，水師並進，克辰州，再進克沅州，並復瀘溪、溆浦、麻陽諸縣。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he directed troops out by separate routes through Fengmu Ridge and Chenlong Pass, with the naval force advancing together, captured Chenzhou, advanced again and captured Yuanzhou, and also recovered Luxi, Xupu, Mayang, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he sent columns through Fengmu Ridge and Chenlong Pass while the fleet moved in parallel, took Chenzhou, then Yuanzhou, and recovered Luxi, Xupu, Mayang, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 大將軍貝子彰泰與會師，自沅州入貴州境。

translations.literal: Grand General Prince Zhangtai joined forces with him and entered Guizhou from Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Prince Zhangtai joined him and entered Guizhou from Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 彰泰疏言綠旗兵已與滿洲兵會，若各自調遣，慮未能合力奏功。

translations.literal: Zhangtai memorialized that the Green Standard troops had already joined the Manchu forces, and if each were dispatched separately he feared they could not combine strength to achieve success.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangtai wrote that Green and Manchu troops were now united and that separate commands might prevent them from fighting as one effective force.

sentences.zh: 上命毓榮軍機關白大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yurong's military plans to be reported to the grand general.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yurong to coordinate his plans with the grand general.

sentences.zh: 尋與衛國督兵克鎮遠、思南。

translations.literal: Soon with Weiguo he directed troops to capture Zhenyuan and Sinan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Weiguo in taking Zhenyuan and Sinan.

sentences.zh: 世璠將夏國相等以二萬人屯平遠西南山，分兵據江西坡，坡天險，國相為像陣。

translations.literal: Shifan's general Xia Guoxiang and others with twenty thousand men encamped on the southwest hills of Pingyuan, divided troops to hold Jiangxi Slope, a slope of natural strategic strength where Guoxiang formed an elephant array.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan's general Xia Guoxiang camped twenty thousand men on the hills southwest of Pingyuan and posted detachments on Jiangxi Slope, a natural strongpoint where Guoxiang deployed an elephant formation.

sentences.zh: 我師迫險攻象陣，不能克，毓榮以紅旗督戰，眾奔不可止，師敗績。

translations.literal: Our army pressed the defile to attack the elephant array but could not overcome it; Yurong supervised battle with the red banner, the masses fled and could not be stopped, and the army suffered a major defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops attacked the elephant line up the slope but failed to break it; Yurong waved the red battle flag to urge them on, yet the ranks broke and could not be rallied, and the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 越二日復戰，鼓眾奮進，國相棄險走，遂克貴陽。

translations.literal: Two days later they fought again; he roused the masses to press forward fiercely, Guoxiang abandoned the defile and fled, and Guiyang was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they fought again; Yurong rallied the men to charge, Guoxiang abandoned the pass and fled, and Guiyang fell.

sentences.zh: 二十年，從彰泰下雲南，次曲靖。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he followed Zhangtai south into Yunnan and halted at Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he marched into Yunnan with Zhangtai and encamped at Qujing.

sentences.zh: 會師進薄會城，屯歸化寺，奪重關及太平橋。

translations.literal: The united armies advanced to press the provincial capital, encamped at Guihua Temple, and seized the major passes and Taiping Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The combined armies closed on the provincial capital, camped at Guihua Temple, and took the main passes and Taiping Bridge.

sentences.zh: 世璠將餘從龍等出降，诇知其虛實。

translations.literal: Shifan's generals Yu Conglong and others came out to surrender, and through reconnaissance they learned the enemy's true strength.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan's officers Yu Conglong and others surrendered, revealing the city's true condition.

sentences.zh: 趙良棟師至，趣進攻，毓榮軍大東門。

translations.literal: When Zhao Liangdong's army arrived he urged an immediate assault; Yurong's force attacked the Great East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangdong arrived and pressed for an immediate assault; Yurong's troops assaulted the Great East Gate.

sentences.zh: 世璠自殺，城下。

translations.literal: Shifan killed himself and the city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan took his own life and the city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 雲南平。

translations.literal: Yunnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 毓榮還任湖廣總督。

translations.literal: Yurong returned to his post as Huguang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Yurong resumed office as governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 累疏區畫善後諸事：「一曰蠲荒賦。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to lay out matters of postwar settlement: "First, remit taxes on wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a series of memorials on postwar recovery: "First, remit taxes on abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 雲南陷寇八載，按畝加糧。

translations.literal: Yunnan was in rebel hands for eight years and grain was levied by the mu.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan had been under the rebels for eight years, with grain levied field by field.

sentences.zh: 驅之鋒鏑，地曠丁稀，無徵地丁。

translations.literal: The people were driven into battle; the land lies vast and households sparse, and there is nothing from which to collect land and poll taxes.
translations.idiomatic: War had emptied the countryside; fields lie fallow and households are few, so land and poll taxes cannot be collected.

sentences.zh: 額賦應予蠲除，招徠開墾。

translations.literal: The scheduled tax quotas should be remitted and settlers recruited to open cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Scheduled quotas should be cancelled and settlers recruited to reopen the land.

sentences.zh: 二曰制土夷。

translations.literal: Second, regulate the native chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Second, regulate the native chieftains.

sentences.zh: 前此土目世職，不過宣慰，三桂濫加至將軍、總兵。

translations.literal: Formerly hereditary native offices went no higher than pacification commissioner; Sangui recklessly promoted them to general and regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary native offices had never ranked above pacification commissioner until Sangui recklessly promoted chiefs to general and regional commander.

sentences.zh: 初投誠，權用偽銜給劄，今當改給土職。

translations.literal: When they first submitted, rebel titles were used provisionally in issuing patents; now proper native offices should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: At first surrender rebel titles were used provisionally; they should now receive proper native offices.

sentences.zh: 舊為三桂奪職者，察明予襲。

translations.literal: Those whose offices Sangui had taken away should be investigated and allowed succession.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom Sangui had deprived of office should be identified and allowed to inherit their posts.

sentences.zh: 三曰靖逋逃。

translations.literal: Third, pacify fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Third, pacify fugitives.

sentences.zh: 三桂舊部奉裁，徵兵散失。

translations.literal: Sangui's old subordinates obeyed the order to disband, and conscripted troops scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's old followers were ordered to disband and conscripts scattered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 八旗僕從，兔脫鼠竄。

translations.literal: Eight Banner retainers fled like rabbits released or rats scurrying away.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Banner bondsmen slipped away like rabbits and rats.

sentences.zh: 宜厚自首賞，重懲窩隱。

translations.literal: Generous rewards should be given for voluntary surrender and heavy penalties for harboring fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Offer generous rewards for surrender and punish harboring severely.

sentences.zh: 所獲逃人，量從末減，庶聞風自歸。

translations.literal: Captured fugitives should be punished at the lighter end of the scale so that others hearing of it will return of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Captured fugitives should receive the lightest penalties so others will come in of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 四曰理財源。

translations.literal: Fourth, regulate sources of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, restore revenue.

sentences.zh: 雲南賦稅不足供兵食。

translations.literal: Yunnan's taxes and levies are insufficient to supply the army's provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's taxes cannot feed the army.

sentences.zh: 地產五金，令民開採，官總其稅。

translations.literal: The land produces the five metals; let the people open mines and the government collect the tax in gross.
translations.idiomatic: The province yields the five metals; let private mining proceed under state collection of tax.

sentences.zh: 省會及祿豐、蒙自、大理設爐鑄錢。

translations.literal: At the provincial capital and at Lufeng, Mengzi, and Dali establish mints to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Establish mints at the capital, Lufeng, Mengzi, and Dali.

sentences.zh: 故明沐氏莊田及入官叛產，均令變價，以裕錢本。

translations.literal: The Ming-era estate lands of the Mu clan and rebel property confiscated by the state should all be sold to enlarge the capital stock for coinage.
translations.idiomatic: Sell the former Ming Mu clan estates and confiscated rebel property to enlarge the coinage reserve.

sentences.zh: 田仍如例納賦，兵弁餘丁，墾荒起科，編入里甲，俾賦有餘而餉可節。

translations.literal: Fields should still pay tax as usual; surplus sons of officers and soldiers should reclaim wasteland and begin taxation, be registered in li and jia, so that tax revenue will be ample and military rations can be economized.
translations.idiomatic: Tax surviving fields as usual; have officers' surplus sons reclaim wasteland, begin taxation, and register in local units so revenue grows and military costs shrink.

sentences.zh: 五曰酌安插。

translations.literal: Fifth, weigh resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, weigh resettlement policy.

sentences.zh: 逆屬嘗隨伍，當遣發極邊。

translations.literal: Rebel dependents who once followed the ranks should be sent to the farthest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel dependents who served in rebel ranks should be sent to the far frontier.

sentences.zh: 若僅受偽銜，並未助逆，宜免遷徙。

translations.literal: If they merely received rebel titles and did not aid the rebellion, they should be exempted from relocation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held rebel titles only and did not aid the rebellion should be spared relocation.

sentences.zh: 六曰收軍仗。

translations.literal: Sixth, collect weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, collect weapons.

sentences.zh: 私造軍器，應坐謀叛論罪。

translations.literal: Private manufacture of weapons should be punished under the statute for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Private arms manufacture should be punished as treason.

sentences.zh: 土司藏刀槍，民以鉛硝、硫黃貿易，皆嚴禁。

translations.literal: Native chieftains hoarding blades and spears, and commoners trading in saltpeter and sulfur, should all be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Strictly forbid native chiefs from hoarding arms and commoners from trading in saltpeter and sulfur.

sentences.zh: 七曰勸捐輸。

translations.literal: Seventh, encourage contributions.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, encourage charitable contributions.

sentences.zh: 雲南民鮮蓋藏，偶有災祲，無從告糴。

translations.literal: The people of Yunnan have little stored wealth; when disaster or famine strikes occasionally, they have no means to seek grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's people keep little in reserve; when disaster strikes they have nowhere to buy grain.

sentences.zh: 請暫開捐監事例。

translations.literal: He requested that the precedent for purchase of supervisory student status be opened temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that purchase of student status be opened temporarily.

sentences.zh: 八曰弭野盜。

translations.literal: Eighth, suppress wild bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, suppress frontier bandits.

sentences.zh: 魯魁在萬山中，初為新習阿蒙土人所據，嘯聚為盜。

translations.literal: Lu Kui lies deep in the myriad mountains; it was first held by the newly converted Ameng natives, who gathered in bands as brigands.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kui lies deep in the mountains; newly converted Ameng tribesmen seized it and formed bandit bands.

sentences.zh: 內通新平、開化、元江、易門，外接車裡、孟艮、鎮元、猛緬。

translations.literal: Within it connects to Xinping, Kaihua, Yuanjiang, and Yimen; without it adjoins Cheli, Menggen, Zhenyuan, and Mengmian.
translations.idiomatic: Inland it links Xinping, Kaihua, Yuanjiang, and Yimen; outward it borders Cheli, Menggen, Zhenyuan, and Mengmian.

sentences.zh: 三桂授以偽職，今雖改授土司。

translations.literal: Sangui granted them rebel offices; though they have now been given native chieftain status.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui had given them rebel titles; they have now been made native chiefs.

sentences.zh: 仍宜厚集土練，分駐隘口，防侵軼為患。

translations.literal: It is still fitting to assemble native militia in strength, post them at the passes in division, and guard against raids as a source of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Native militia should still be concentrated and posted at the passes to block raids.

sentences.zh: 九曰敦實政。

translations.literal: Ninth, promote solid administration.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, promote sound local government.

sentences.zh: 兵後整理撫綏，其要在墾荒蕪，廣樹蓄，裕積貯，興教化，嚴保甲，通商賈，崇節儉，蠲雜派，卹無告，止濫差。

translations.literal: After the war, putting order and pacification in place depends on reclaiming wasteland, widely planting and storing, enriching reserves, reviving education, tightening baojia, opening commerce, honoring frugality, remitting miscellaneous levies, relieving the destitute, and stopping abusive requisitions.
translations.idiomatic: Postwar recovery depends on reclaiming wasteland, planting and storing grain, building reserves, reviving schools, tightening baojia security, encouraging trade, practicing frugality, cutting miscellaneous levies, aiding the destitute, and ending abusive requisitions.

sentences.zh: 州縣吏即以此十事為殿最。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county officials should be ranked superior or inferior on these ten matters.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county officials should be judged on these ten points.

sentences.zh: 十曰舉廢墜。

translations.literal: Tenth, restore what has fallen into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, restore what has fallen into ruin.

sentences.zh: 各府州縣學宮，自三桂煽亂，悉皆頹壞。

translations.literal: The Confucian schools of every prefecture, department, and county, since Sangui stirred rebellion, have all collapsed in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian schools in every prefecture and county have lain in ruins since Sangui's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今宜倡率修復。

translations.literal: Now one ought to take the lead in advocating restoration.
translations.idiomatic: At present the court should take the lead in promoting repair and recovery.

sentences.zh: 通省稅糧，既有成額，宜均本折定，留運驛站，酌加工食，俾民間永無派累。」

translations.literal: For tax grain throughout the province, since fixed quotas already exist, the rates for payment in grain and commutation should be set uniformly; funds should be reserved for transport and courier stations, and processing fees for rations added as appropriate, so that the people may never again suffer extra levies."
translations.idiomatic: Provincial tax grain already has fixed quotas; rates for grain tribute and commutation should be set uniformly, with provision kept for transport and courier stations and a modest allowance added for milling and rations, so that the people are never again burdened by special assessments.

sentences.zh: 疏入，廷臣議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the court ministers deliberated and ordered it carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received, and the court deliberated and approved its implementation.

sentences.zh: 別疏言：「督標舊額兵四千，請增千為五營。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he stated: 'The governor-general's established quota of troops is four thousand; I request that one thousand be added, making five battalions.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: 'The governor-general's standing force numbers four thousand men; I ask that one thousand more be added to form five battalions.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂設十鎮，今改為六。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui had established ten garrison commands; these are now to be reduced to six.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had created ten garrison commands; these are now to be reorganized as six.

sentences.zh: 在迤西者：曰鶴麗、曰永順、曰楚姚蒙景，在迤東者：曰開​​化、曰臨元澂江、曰曲尋武霑。」

translations.literal: Those in the far west are called Heli, Yongshun, and Chuyao-Mengjing; those in the far east are called Kaihua, Linyuan-Chengjiang, and Quzun-Wuzhan.'
translations.idiomatic: In the far west there were Heli, Yongshun, and the Chuyao-Mengjing command; in the far east, Kaihua, Linyuan-Chengjiang, and Quzun-Wuzhan.'

sentences.zh: 「中甸舊轄麗江土府，三桂割畀蒙、番互市。

translations.literal: 'Zhongdian was formerly under the native prefecture of Lijiang; Sangui had ceded it for trade with the Mongols and Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdian had formerly been under the Lijiang native prefecture; Sangui had carved it out and assigned it for Mongol and Tibetan border trade.

sentences.zh: 今互市已停，蒙、番所設喇嘛營官未撤，宜令土知府木堯仍歸其地。」

translations.literal: Now that the border market has been suspended, the lama-camp officials set up by the Mongols and Tibetans have not yet been withdrawn; the native prefect Mu Yao should be ordered to resume jurisdiction over that territory.'
translations.idiomatic: Border trade has now ceased, yet the lama-camp officials established by the Mongols and Tibetans remain in place; Mu Yao, the native prefect, should be restored to his former jurisdiction.'

sentences.zh: 初，師自貴州下雲南，毓榮劾董衛國不聽調度，上命俟事平再議。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the army marched from Guizhou into Yunnan, Yurong impeached Dong Weiguo for disobeying orders; the Emperor ordered that the matter be reconsidered only after affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the army first advanced from Guizhou into Yunnan, Yurong impeached Dong Weiguo for refusing to obey orders; the Emperor directed that the case be held over until the campaign was concluded.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，部議衛國未嘗違誤，且有復鎮遠功，請免議，上責毓榮妒功誣奏，下部議，削五級。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the ministry reported that Weiguo had never been derelict and had merit in recovering Zhenyuan, and requested that the inquiry be waived; the Emperor rebuked Yurong for jealous slander, referred the matter to the ministry, and reduced Yurong by five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the ministry found that Weiguo had committed no fault and had distinguished himself in recovering Zhenyuan, and asked that the charge be dropped; the Emperor condemned Yurong for jealous false accusation, referred the case to the ministry, and stripped him of five ranks.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，授總督倉場侍郎，改兵部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister in charge of the granaries under the governor-general, then transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was made Vice Minister of Granaries under the governor-general, and later transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 領侍衛內大臣佟國維等疏言侍衛納爾泰自陳前使雲南，毓榮令其子琳餽以銀九百；

translations.literal: Senior Bodyguard and Inner Minister Tong Guowei and others memorialized that the bodyguard Naertai had confessed that on an earlier mission to Yunnan, Yurong had his son Lin present him with nine hundred taels of silver;
translations.idiomatic: Senior Bodyguard and Inner Minister Tong Guowei and others reported that the bodyguard Naertai had confessed that during an earlier mission to Yunnan, Yurong had his son Lin give him nine hundred taels of silver;

sentences.zh: 內務府又發毓榮入雲南以三桂女孫為妾，並徇縱逆黨狀：下刑部，鞫實，擬斬，籍沒，命免死，與琳並戍黑龍江。

translations.literal: the Imperial Household Department also exposed that after Yurong entered Yunnan he took Wu Sangui's granddaughter as a concubine and indulged rebel partisans; the case was sent to the Ministry of Justice, investigation confirmed the facts, and death with confiscation of property was recommended; the Emperor spared his life and exiled him together with Lin to Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Household Department further disclosed that after entering Yunnan Yurong had taken Wu Sangui's granddaughter as a concubine and had knowingly sheltered rebel associates; the case went to the Ministry of Justice, where the facts were established and death with confiscation of property was proposed; the Emperor commuted the sentence, and Yurong and Lin were banished to Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 赦還。

translations.literal: He was pardoned and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: He was later pardoned and permitted to return.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-eighth year.

sentences.zh: 哈佔，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Hazhan, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a bondsman of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan, of the Irgen Gioro clan, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 自官學生授鴻臚寺贊禮郎，累遷兵部督捕理事官。

translations.literal: From a student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed Director of Ceremonies at the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and was promoted in succession to the post of supervising officer for military pursuit in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a student of the Imperial Academy, he was appointed Director of Ceremonies at the Court of Imperial Entertainments and rose in succession to supervising officer for military pursuit in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，授秘書院學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was appointed an academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Kangxi reign he was made an academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授陝西總督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Governor-General of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed Governor-General of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 甫到官，吳三桂反，四川提督鄭蛟麟、總兵吳之茂等叛應之，與三桂將王屏籓謀寇陝西。

translations.literal: Hardly had he assumed office when Wu Sangui rebelled; the Sichuan Provincial Commander Zheng Jiaolin, Regional Commander Wu Zhimao, and others rose in response, and together with Sangui's general Wang Pingfan plotted to invade Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely taken office when Wu Sangui rebelled; Sichuan Provincial Commander Zheng Jiaolin, Regional Commander Wu Zhimao, and others joined the revolt, and with Sangui's general Wang Pingfan they plotted an invasion of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 上授都統赫業安西將軍，會西安將軍瓦爾喀討之，命哈佔與巡撫杭愛督餉，並敕與提督張勇、王輔臣修邊備，輯軍民。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Commander Heye General Pacifying the West, and together with the Xi'an General Wuerka marched to suppress them; Hazhan and the Censor-in-Chief Hang Ai were ordered to supervise supplies, and Hazhan was also commanded, together with Provincial Commanders Zhang Yong and Wang Fuchen, to repair frontier defenses and restore order among soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed Commander Heye General Pacifying the West and, together with Xi'an General Wuerka, sent him to suppress the rebels; Hazhan and Censor-in-Chief Hang Ai were ordered to supervise provisions, and Hazhan was further instructed, together with Provincial Commanders Zhang Yong and Wang Fuchen, to strengthen the frontier and restore order among troops and people.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復命尚書莫洛經略陝西，敕凡事諮哈佔乃行。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Minister Moluo was again appointed to oversee Shaanxi, with orders that all affairs were to be carried out only after consulting Hazhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Minister Moluo was again appointed to direct affairs in Shaanxi, with instructions that nothing was to be done without Hazhan's counsel.

sentences.zh: 哈佔以漢中、廣元山迳險峻，疏請造船略陽速糧運。

translations.literal: Hazhan, noting that the mountain routes through Hanzhong and Guangyuan were steep and perilous, memorialized requesting that boats be built at Lueyang to speed grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Because the mountain routes through Hanzhong and Guangyuan were steep and dangerous, Hazhan memorialized asking that boats be built at Lueyang to expedite grain transport.

sentences.zh: 尋又命貝勒董額為定西大將軍，護諸將出秦州，徇四川。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Prince Dong'e was appointed Grand General Pacifying the West, leading the generals out from Qinzhou toward Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Prince Dong'e was appointed Grand General Pacifying the West and led the generals out from Qinzhou into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 寇劫略陽糧艘，上命四川總督周有德督川境轉餉。

translations.literal: Bandits plundered the grain boats at Lueyang; the Emperor ordered the Sichuan Governor-General Zhou Youde to supervise the transfer of supplies within Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels raided the grain convoys at Lueyang; the Emperor ordered Sichuan Governor-General Zhou Youde to oversee the relay of supplies within Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 哈佔疏請令山西協助，上以山西道遠多勞費，發帑十五萬，使在西安採運；

translations.literal: Hazhan memorialized requesting that Shanxi assist; the Emperor, considering that Shanxi was far away and the effort costly, disbursed one hundred fifty thousand taels from the treasury and had supplies procured and transported from Xi'an;
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan memorialized asking that Shanxi lend assistance; the Emperor, judging the Shanxi route too distant and costly, released one hundred fifty thousand taels from the treasury and ordered supplies gathered and transported from Xi'an;

sentences.zh: 並諭宜稍增其直，俾民樂輸送。

translations.literal: he also instructed that the transport price be slightly increased so that the people would willingly deliver supplies.
translations.idiomatic: he also directed that transport rates be raised somewhat so that the people would willingly carry the supplies.

sentences.zh: 會輔臣叛，莫洛遇害。

translations.literal: Then Wang Fuchen rebelled, and Moluo was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Fuchen rebelled, and Moluo was slain.

sentences.zh: 董額以餉不繼，自漢中引還西安。

translations.literal: Because supplies could not be maintained, Dong'e withdrew from Hanzhong back to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies failed to keep up, Dong'e withdrew from Hanzhong to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔哈佔分兵防蘭州，哈佔疏言西安兵少不宜分遣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict ordered Hazhan to detach troops to defend Lanzhou; Hazhan memorialized that Xi'an had too few troops and that none should be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the court ordered Hazhan to detach troops for the defense of Lanzhou; Hazhan replied that Xi'an's garrison was too small and that troops should not be divided.

sentences.zh: 上命雲貴總督鄂善率師駐興安、漢中，既又命守延安，哈佔迭奏請留西安不遣。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Eshan to lead troops to garrison Xing'an and Hanzhong; he then also ordered him to hold Yan'an, but Hazhan repeatedly memorialized asking that Eshan be kept at Xi'an and not dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Eshan to lead troops to garrison Xing'an and Hanzhong, and later commanded him to hold Yan'an as well; Hazhan repeatedly asked that Eshan be kept at Xi'an and not sent out.

sentences.zh: 時輔臣據平涼，同州游擊李師膺叛，戕韓城知縣翟世琪，脅神道嶺營卒，合蒲城土寇陷延安。

translations.literal: At that time Fuchen held Pingliang; the Tongzhou brigade commander Li Shiying rebelled, killed Hancheng Magistrate Zhai Shiqi, coerced the soldiers at the Shendaoling camp, and together with local bandits from Pucheng captured Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fuchen held Pingliang; Tongzhou brigade commander Li Shiying rebelled, murdered Hancheng Magistrate Zhai Shiqi, forced the garrison at Shendaoling into service, and together with bandits from Pucheng seized Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 固原道陳彭、定邊副將硃龍皆以城叛。

translations.literal: Circuit Intendant Chen Peng of Guyuan and Vice Commander Zhu Long of Dingbian both rebelled with their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Peng, the Guyuan circuit intendant, and Zhu Long, vice commander at Dingbian, both turned their cities over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 輔臣分兵四出，陷旁近諸州縣，遂破蘭州，巡撫華善走涼州。

translations.literal: Fuchen sent his forces out on four fronts, captured the neighboring prefectures and counties, and then took Lanzhou; Governor Huashan fled to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen divided his forces and struck on four fronts, overrunning the neighboring prefectures and counties before finally taking Lanzhou; Governor Huashan fled to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣將逐賊邠州、淳化、三水、長武、漢陰、石泉、甘泉、寶雞諸處，戰輒勝。

translations.literal: He sent generals to pursue the rebels through Binzhou, Chunhua, Sanshui, Changwu, Hanyin, Shiquan, Ganquan, Baoji, and other places, winning every engagement.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched generals to drive the rebels from Binzhou, Chunhua, Sanshui, Changwu, Hanyin, Shiquan, Ganquan, Baoji, and other districts, winning every battle.

sentences.zh: 董額師克秦州，總兵王進寶亦復蘭州。

translations.literal: Dong'e's army captured Qinzhou, and Regional Commander Wang Jinbao also recovered Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'e's army took Qinzhou, and Regional Commander Wang Jinbao recovered Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 定邊、延安皆下。

translations.literal: Dingbian and Yan'an were both recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Dingbian and Yan'an were both retaken.

sentences.zh: 上趣董額督兵合攻平涼。

translations.literal: The Emperor urged Dong'e to lead the armies in a joint assault on Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pressed Dong'e to concentrate his forces and attack Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 哈佔聞興安游擊王可成叛，移潼關綠旗兵守商州，移西安滿洲兵守潼關。

translations.literal: Hazhan, hearing that the Xing'an brigade commander Wang Kecheng had rebelled, moved the Green Standard troops at Tongguan to defend Shangzhou and shifted the Manchu troops at Xi'an to hold Tongguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hazhan learned that Xing'an brigade commander Wang Kecheng had rebelled, he moved the Green Standard garrison at Tongguan to Shangzhou and shifted Xi'an's Manchu troops to hold Tongguan.

sentences.zh: 俄聞興安叛兵已破商州舊縣關，逼西安，疏請敕董額分兵赴援。

translations.literal: Soon he heard that the rebel troops from Xing'an had broken through the old county pass at Shangzhou and were pressing on Xi'an; he memorialized requesting an edict that Dong'e detach troops to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he learned that the Xing'an rebels had broken through the old county pass at Shangzhou and were threatening Xi'an; he memorialized asking that Dong'e be ordered to send a detachment to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 上責哈占曰：「輔臣初叛，朕以蘭州近邊要地，令哈佔發兵鎮守。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Hazhan, saying: 'When Fuchen first rebelled, I, considering Lanzhou a vital frontier stronghold, ordered Hazhan to dispatch troops to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked Hazhan, saying: 'When Fuchen first rebelled, I judged Lanzhou a critical frontier post and ordered Hazhan to send troops to defend it.

sentences.zh: 哈佔以西安兵少不遣，蘭州遂陷。

translations.literal: Hazhan, claiming that Xi'an had too few troops, refused to send any, and Lanzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan, pleading that Xi'an's garrison was too small, refused to detach men, and Lanzhou was lost.

sentences.zh: 又以延安居要衝，命鄂善屯守，哈佔留之西安，延安复陷。

translations.literal: Then, because Yan'an occupied a strategic crossroads, I ordered Eshan to garrison it, but Hazhan kept him at Xi'an, and Yan'an fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Then, because Yan'an lay on a vital route, I ordered Eshan to hold it, but Hazhan kept him at Xi'an, and Yan'an fell once more.

sentences.zh: 哈佔但知有西安，重兵自衛，貽誤非小！」

translations.literal: Hazhan knows only Xi'an, hoards troops to protect himself, and the harm he has done is no small matter!'
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan cares for nothing but Xi'an, keeps his main force for his own protection, and the damage he has caused is grave!'

sentences.zh: 別敕董額急攻平涼，仍遣將軍吳丹率師自太原移駐潼關，員外郎拉篤祜率榆林蒙古兵益西安。

translations.literal: In a separate edict Dong'e was ordered to press the attack on Pingliang; General Wu Dan was still sent from Taiyuan to garrison Tongguan, and Department Director Laduhu was sent with Mongol troops from Yulin to reinforce Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate order Dong'e was commanded to press the assault on Pingliang; General Wu Dan was sent from Taiyuan to garrison Tongguan, and Department Director Laduhu was dispatched with Mongol troops from Yulin to reinforce Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大學士圖海代董額為大將軍，圍平涼，輔臣降。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Grand Secretary Tu Hai replaced Dong'e as Grand General, besieged Pingliang, and Fuchen surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Grand Secretary Tu Hai replaced Dong'e as Grand General, besieged Pingliang, and Fuchen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 哈佔疏請安輯降眾，設置官吏。

translations.literal: Hazhan memorialized requesting that the surrendered masses be pacified and officials appointed to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan memorialized asking that the surrendered population be settled and local officials appointed.

sentences.zh: 事皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All these matters were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Each proposal was referred to the ministries for deliberation and approved for execution.

sentences.zh: 十九年，將軍趙良棟克成都，王進寶克保寧，郡縣以次底定。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year General Zhao Liangdong captured Chengdu, Wang Jinbao captured Baoning, and the prefectures and counties were pacified in turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year General Zhao Liangdong took Chengdu and Wang Jinbao took Baoning; prefecture after prefecture and county after county were brought back under control.

sentences.zh: 哈佔疏言軍餉自西安運保寧，應令四川接運。

translations.literal: Hazhan memorialized that military supplies transported from Xi'an to Baoning ought to be relayed by Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan memorialized that grain transported from Xi'an to Baoning should be taken over and relayed within Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 上以四川初定，未能任轉餉，命自略陽水道運敘州。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering that Sichuan had only just been pacified and could not yet bear the burden of relay transport, ordered that supplies be moved by the Lueyang water route to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, judging that Sichuan had only just been pacified and could not yet manage relay transport, ordered supplies carried by the Lueyang water route to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋敕哈佔率師赴保寧，規復雲南。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hazhan was ordered to lead his army to Baoning to plan the recovery of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hazhan was commanded to march to Baoning and prepare the reconquest of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 哈佔复疏請命四川督餉，戶部侍郎趙璟、金鼐疏言陝西轉餉入四川，四川吏不之卹，道遠民滋困。

translations.literal: Hazhan again memorialized requesting that Sichuan be put in charge of supplies; Vice Ministers of Revenue Zhao Jing and Jin Tai memorialized that when Shaanxi relayed provisions into Sichuan, Sichuan officials showed no concern, and because the route was long the people grew ever more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan again asked that Sichuan be charged with supply duties; Vice Ministers of Revenue Zhao Jing and Jin Tai reported that when Shaanxi forwarded provisions into Sichuan, Sichuan officials paid little heed, and the long haul only wore the people down further.

sentences.zh: 尚書宋德宜言陝西、四川宜以一總督董理，庶兩省民勞逸得平，乃改設川陝總督，以命哈佔。

translations.literal: Minister Song Deyi said that Shaanxi and Sichuan ought to be overseen by a single governor-general so that the labor and rest of the people in both provinces might be balanced; thereupon the post of Governor-General of Sichuan and Shaanxi was created, and Hazhan was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Song Deyi argued that Shaanxi and Sichuan should be governed by one governor-general, so that the burdens borne by the people of both provinces might be equalized; the post of Governor-General of Sichuan and Shaanxi was therefore created, and Hazhan was appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 哈佔師次保寧，時叛將譚弘、彭時亨四出劫掠為民害，上命速剿定，進攻雲南。

translations.literal: When Hazhan's army halted at Baoning, the rebel generals Tan Hong and Peng Shiheng were raiding in all directions and harming the people; the Emperor ordered that they be swiftly suppressed and pacified, and that the advance on Yunnan proceed.
translations.idiomatic: While Hazhan's army was encamped at Baoning, the rebel generals Tan Hong and Peng Shiheng were marauding on every side and preying on the people; the Emperor ordered them crushed without delay and commanded the advance on Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 哈佔遣總兵高孟擊時亨，敗賊南溪羅石橋，复營山、渠二縣。

translations.literal: Hazhan sent Regional Commander Gao Meng to attack Shiheng, defeated the rebels at Luoshi Bridge in Nanxi, and recovered the two counties of Yingshan and Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan dispatched Regional Commander Gao Meng against Shiheng, routed the rebels at Luoshi Bridge in Nanxi, and recovered Yingshan and Qu.

sentences.zh: 二十年，鎮南將軍噶爾漢收忠、萬、開、建始、雲陽、梁山諸州縣。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year General Pacifying the South Ga'erhan recovered Zhong, Wan, Kai, Jianshi, Yunyang, Liangshan, and other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year General Pacifying the South Ga'erhan retook Zhong, Wan, Kai, Jianshi, Yunyang, Liangshan, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 弘走死。

translations.literal: Hong fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hong fled and perished.

sentences.zh: 孟逐時亨，亦復廣安、達、大竹、東鄉諸州縣。

translations.literal: Meng pursued Shiheng and also recovered Guang'an, Da, Dazhu, Dongxiang, and other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Meng pursued Shiheng and likewise recovered Guang'an, Da, Dazhu, Dongxiang, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 時亨勢蹙，降。

translations.literal: Shiheng, pressed hard, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Shiheng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 敕哈佔率師赴敘州，會建昌、永寧兩路兵進徵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hazhan to lead his army to Xuzhou and join the forces of the Jianchang and Yongning routes in the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan was ordered to march to Xuzhou and unite with the armies of the Jianchang and Yongning routes for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 哈佔師發永寧，追擊三桂將馬進寶，入貴州。

translations.literal: Hazhan's army set out from Yongning, pursued Sangui's general Ma Jinbao, and entered Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan's army marched from Yongning, pursued Sangui's general Ma Jinbao, and entered Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 次畢節，進寶降。

translations.literal: Halting at Bijie, he accepted Jinbao's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Bijie he accepted Jinbao's surrender.

sentences.zh: 復進次威寧。

translations.literal: He advanced again and halted at Weining.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on and encamped at Weining.

sentences.zh: 大將軍貝子彰泰疏言雲南已合圍，師足用，兵多糧少，宜令哈佔還四川。

translations.literal: Grand General Prince Zhangtai memorialized that Yunnan was already fully invested, that the troops on hand were sufficient, and that with many soldiers but little grain Hazhan ought to be ordered back to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Prince Zhangtai reported that Yunnan was already encircled, that the forces there were sufficient, and that with too many men and too little grain Hazhan should be recalled to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 哈佔復進次曲靖，聞命引還。

translations.literal: Hazhan advanced again and halted at Qujing; on receiving the order he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan had already advanced to Qujing when the order arrived, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 尋以破時亨功，加兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for his merit in defeating Shiheng, he was given the rank of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for his success against Shiheng, he was granted the honorary rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 弘將牟一乾、一舉詣遵義降，分駐巴縣、涪州。

translations.literal: Hong's generals Mou Yiqian and Yiju came to Zunyi to surrender and were posted separately at Baxian and Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's generals Mou Yiqian and Yiju surrendered at Zunyi and were stationed separately at Baxian and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 哈佔疏請移陝西，懦者歸農，強者入伍，上從之。

translations.literal: Hazhan memorialized requesting that they be moved to Shaanxi, the weak returned to farming and the strong enrolled in the army; the Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan asked that these men be resettled in Shaanxi, with the weak sent back to the fields and the strong enlisted; the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞休，上疏自述在軍時積勞成病。

translations.literal: Citing illness, he requested retirement and memorialized that the accumulated hardships of his years in the field had brought on his sickness.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of illness, memorializing that the accumulated strain of his years in the field had ruined his health.

sentences.zh: 上以哈佔未嘗立功，斥其妄，命仍殫力供職自贖。

translations.literal: The Emperor, saying that Hazhan had never achieved merit, denounced the claim as false and ordered him to continue serving with all his strength to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, declaring that Hazhan had never truly distinguished himself, rejected the plea as pretense and ordered him to remain at his post and serve zealously by way of atonement.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fifth year.

sentences.zh: 杭愛，章佳氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Hang Ai, of the Zhangjia clan, was a bondsman of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Ai, of the Zhangjia clan, belonged to the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父古爾嘉琿，順治初為國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: His father, Gu'erjiagong, served in the early Shunzhi reign as Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu'erjiagong had served in the early Shunzhi reign as Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 杭愛初授筆帖式，累遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Hang Ai was first appointed a clerk and was promoted in succession to Department Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Ai began as a clerk and rose in succession to Department Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，超授山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi he was exceptionally appointed Provincial Treasurer of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Kangxi reign he was promoted directly to Provincial Treasurer of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「朕知汝才能，外省事重，籓司職掌最要。

translations.literal: An edict stated: 'I know your talent and ability; affairs in the outer provinces are weighty, and the duties of a provincial treasurer are especially important.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor instructed him: 'I know your ability; affairs in the provinces are weighty, and the office of provincial treasurer is especially critical.

sentences.zh: 其克盡忠誠，毋負簡任！」

translations.literal: You must devote yourself in full loyalty and not fail this appointment!'
translations.idiomatic: Serve with complete loyalty, and do not betray the trust I place in you!'

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 軍興，命督餉。

translations.literal: When the war began he was ordered to supervise supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When hostilities broke out he was ordered to supervise provisions.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調四川。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 叛將譚弘據萬縣為亂，命杭愛慰撫夔州諸路。

translations.literal: The rebel general Tan Hong had seized Wanxian and risen in revolt; Hang Ai was ordered to pacify the routes around Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel general Tan Hong held Wanxian in rebellion, Hang Ai was ordered to pacify the districts around Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年，建昌土司安泰宁謀亂，敕與將軍王進寶招之來降。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the Jianchang native chieftain An Taining plotted rebellion; Hang Ai was commanded, together with General Wang Jinbao, to summon him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Jianchang native chieftain An Taining plotted rebellion; Hang Ai was ordered, together with General Wang Jinbao, to induce him to submit.

sentences.zh: 哈佔師進次永寧，命杭愛督趣輸運。

translations.literal: When Hazhan's army advanced and halted at Yongning, Hang Ai was ordered to supervise and expedite transport.
translations.idiomatic: When Hazhan's army advanced to Yongning, Hang Ai was ordered to oversee and hurry the delivery of supplies.

sentences.zh: 自三桂亂，四川悉陷，民多流亡，兵佔耕民田不納賦。

translations.literal: Since Sangui's rebellion, all of Sichuan had fallen; many people had fled, and soldiers occupied farmland without paying taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Sangui's revolt all of Sichuan had been overrun; the people had fled in great numbers, and soldiers seized cultivated land without paying tax.

sentences.zh: 杭愛疏請清釐，又乞蠲羅森妄報墾荒昇科田四百餘畝，上特允之。

translations.literal: Hang Ai memorialized requesting a thorough investigation, and also asked that more than four hundred mu of land falsely reported as reclaimed wasteland and upgraded to taxable fields by Luo Sen be remitted; the Emperor specially granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Ai memorialized for a full reckoning of these abuses, and also asked that more than four hundred mu of land falsely reported as newly reclaimed and brought under tax by Luo Sen be exempted; the Emperor granted the request as a special favor.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒，諡勤襄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, and was given the posthumous title Qinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year and was posthumously honored as Qinxiang.

sentences.zh: 鄂善，納喇氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Eshan, of the Nara clan, was a bondsman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Eshan, of the Nara clan, belonged to the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 初自侍衛授秘書院學士，遷副都御史。

translations.literal: He was first appointed from the bodyguard corps as an academician of the Secretariat, then transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from the bodyguard corps, he was appointed an academician of the Secretariat and later made Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，授陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi he was appointed Censor-in-Chief of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Kangxi reign he was appointed Censor-in-Chief of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢山西陝西總督，尋改專督陝西。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Governor-General of Shanxi and Shaanxi, and soon afterward was changed to govern Shaanxi alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Governor-General of Shanxi and Shaanxi, and shortly thereafter was made governor of Shaanxi alone.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調雲南，以哈佔代。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Yunnan and was replaced by Hazhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Yunnan, with Hazhan succeeding him in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，詔鄂善留湖廣。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, an edict ordered Eshan to remain in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui rebelled, the court ordered Eshan to remain in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改兼督雲、貴，命從師進徵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was additionally made governor of Yunnan and Guizhou and ordered to follow the army on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was given joint charge of Yunnan and Guizhou and ordered to march with the expeditionary force.

sentences.zh: 三桂陷湖南郡縣，吏議鐫五級，命留任。

translations.literal: When Sangui captured prefectures and counties in Hunan, the officials deliberated reducing Eshan by five ranks, but the Emperor ordered that he remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangui overran prefectures and counties in Hunan, the ministry proposed demoting Eshan by five ranks, but the Emperor ordered him retained in his post.

sentences.zh: 王輔臣叛，命與副都統穆舒渾率師自襄陽移守興安、漢中。

translations.literal: When Wang Fuchen rebelled, Eshan was ordered, together with Vice Commander Mushuhun, to lead troops from Xiangyang to garrison Xing'an and Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Fuchen rebelled, he was ordered, together with Vice Commander Mushuhun, to lead troops from Xiangyang to hold Xing'an and Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十四年，次西安，哈佔疏留助守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was stationed at Xi'an; Ha Zhan memorialized asking to remain and assist in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he halted at Xi'an, and Ha Zhan memorialized the throne, begging leave to stay and help hold the city.

sentences.zh: 上復命移守榆林、延安，哈佔再疏留不遣。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered him transferred to guard Yulin and Yan'an; Ha Zhan again memorialized to remain and was not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered him to shift his command to Yulin and Yan'an, but Ha Zhan once more memorialized to stay—and was not released from his post.

sentences.zh: 及畢力克圖擊輔臣，复延安，鄂善乃遵上指移駐，招撫流民，分守棧道，寇來犯，擊之退。

translations.literal: When Biliketu attacked Fu Chen and recovered Yan'an, E Shan then followed the emperor's instruction to move his headquarters, pacified displaced people, divided forces to guard the plank roads, and when bandits came to attack, drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Biliketu struck Fu Chen and Yan'an was recovered, E Shan at last obeyed the imperial command to relocate. He pacified the wandering populace, posted troops along the plank roads, and whenever raiders came against him, beat them back.

sentences.zh: 授甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，坐失察布政使伊圖蝕帑、清水知縣佟國佐苛斂，部議當奪官，命留任。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was punished for lack of supervision: Provincial Administration Commissioner Yitu embezzled treasury funds, and Qingshui Magistrate Tong Guozuo levied harsh exactions; the ministry recommended stripping him of office, but he was ordered to remain in his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was held accountable for failing to oversee his subordinates: Provincial Administration Commissioner Yitu had eaten into the treasury, and Qingshui Magistrate Tong Guozuo had squeezed the people with cruel levies. The ministry recommended that he be stripped of rank, but the emperor ordered him retained.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以計典罷。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was dismissed in the regular evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was removed from office in the triennial evaluation.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 華善，亦伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Hua Shan, also of the Irgen Gioro clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Shan, likewise of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授筆帖式，累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a clerk; he rose through successive promotions to Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a clerk and, through successive promotions, rose to Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，從大將軍伊爾德克舟山，累進世職拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, he followed Grand General Yierde to Zhoushan and, through successive advances in hereditary rank, was enfeoffed as Talabuule Han and also Tuoshala Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi he followed Grand General Yierde against Zhoushan, and through repeated advancement in hereditary rank was enfeoffed as Talabuule Han with the additional rank of Tuoshala Han.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，累遷弘文院學士。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi reign, he was repeatedly promoted to Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kangxi reign he rose by stages to Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 九年，授甘肅巡撫，疏請免逃荒額賦。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Governor of Gansu and memorialized requesting exemption of abandoned-land quota taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Governor of Gansu and memorialized to remit the tax quotas imposed on abandoned farmland.

sentences.zh: 西和、禮縣大疫，華善發帑治賑，並以春耕期迫，令市耕牛、具籽種，事竟乃疏聞，部議以違例當責償，上命寬之。

translations.literal: Xihe and Lixian suffered a great epidemic; Hua Shan disbursed treasury funds for treatment and relief, and because the spring plowing season was urgent, ordered purchase of plow oxen and seed grain; only after the matter was finished did he memorialize the throne; the ministry recommended accountability and restitution for violating precedent, but the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When Xihe and Lixian were ravaged by plague, Hua Shan opened the treasury for medicine and relief. The season for spring planting pressed hard upon him, so he ordered oxen bought and seed grain prepared; only when the work was done did he report what he had done. The ministry held that he had violated precedent and ought to make restitution, but the emperor commanded that he be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 輔臣反，攻蘭州，游擊董正己叛應之，布政使成額降寇，華善與按察使伊圖走永昌，疏請假提督張勇便宜討輔臣，與勇及王進寶、陳福、孫思克分道進兵，規复蘭州。

translations.literal: Fu Chen rebelled and attacked Lanzhou; Brigade Commander Dong Zhengji defected in response; Provincial Administration Commissioner Cheng'e surrendered to the rebels; Hua Shan and Regional Inspector Yitu fled to Yongchang; he memorialized requesting discretionary authority for Provincial Commander Zhang Yong to suppress Fu Chen; with Yong, Wang Jinbao, Chen Fu, and Sun Sike he advanced by separate routes, planning to recover Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Chen rose in rebellion and assailed Lanzhou, Brigade Commander Dong Zhengji went over to him, and Provincial Administration Commissioner Cheng'e surrendered to the enemy. Hua Shan fled with Regional Inspector Yitu to Yongchang and memorialized, asking that Provincial Commander Zhang Yong be granted discretionary power to suppress Fu Chen. He then divided his forces with Yong, Wang Jinbao, Chen Fu, and Sun Sike, each marching by a different route with the aim of retaking Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 華善與勇督兵赴臨洮，遣將收河、洮二州，复督兵攻鞏昌，克之，會進寶亦克蘭州，諭嘉勞。

translations.literal: Hua Shan and Yong led troops to Lintao, dispatched generals to recover the He and Tao prefectures, again led troops to attack Gongchang and took it; when Jinbao also took Lanzhou, an edict praised and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Shan and Yong led the army to Lintao and sent generals to recover the prefectures of He and Tao. He then turned again to Gongchang, stormed it, and took the city; when Jinbao likewise recovered Lanzhou, an imperial edict praised their labors and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 十五年，疏請免臨洮、鞏昌二府逋賦。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he memorialized requesting remission of tax arrears for the two prefectures of Lintao and Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he memorialized to remit the overdue taxes of Lintao and Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於官。

translations.literal: Soon after, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 董衛國，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Dong Weiguo, a Han bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Weiguo was a Han bannerman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授佐領，累官秘書院學士。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed an Assistant Commandant; he rose through successive posts to Academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He first received appointment as an Assistant Commandant and rose by degrees to Academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 順治十八年，擢山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Shunzhi he was promoted to Governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Shunzhi he was elevated to Governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，加工部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi he was given the additional title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kangxi he was granted the additional rank of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the title was changed to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his additional rank was changed to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，陷長沙，衛國疏請發兵備袁州、吉安，上命副都統根特自兗州移兵赴援。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled and took Changsha; Weiguo memorialized requesting troops sent to prepare Yuanzhou and Ji'an; the emperor ordered Vice Commander-in-chief Gent to move troops from Yanzhou to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled and Changsha fell, Weiguo memorialized that troops be sent to ready the defenses of Yuanzhou and Ji'an. The emperor ordered Vice Commander-in-chief Gent to shift his forces from Yanzhou to the relief.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠亦反，侵寧都、廣昌、南豐諸府縣，饒州參將程鳳、廣信副將柯升叛應之，構土寇破都昌，窺南康。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong also rebelled, invading Ningdu, Guangchang, Nanfeng and other prefectures and counties; Raozhou Brigade Commander Cheng Feng and Guangxin Vice Commander Ke Sheng defected in response; they recruited local bandits, took Duchang, and eyed Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong rebelled as well, overrunning Ningdu, Guangchang, Nanfeng, and other districts. Raozhou Brigade Commander Cheng Feng and Guangxin Vice Commander Ke Sheng went over to him; they stirred up local bandits, broke Duchang, and turned their gaze toward Nankang.

sentences.zh: 衛國密疏聞，上命定南將軍希爾根會衛國剿禦。

translations.literal: Weiguo sent a secret memorial; the emperor ordered Pacification General of the South Xiergen to join Weiguo in suppression and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Weiguo sent a secret memorial apprising the throne, and the emperor ordered Pacification General of the South Xiergen to unite with Weiguo in suppression and defense.

sentences.zh: 精忠兵逼袁州，山民棚居與相結，謂之「棚寇」。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's troops pressed Yuanzhou; mountain dwellers living in sheds allied with them—these were called 'Shed Bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's army pressed upon Yuanzhou, where mountain folk dwelling in rough shelters joined them; such men were called the Shed Bandits.

sentences.zh: 衛國請設袁臨總兵，薦副將趙應奎有膽略堪任，上從之。

translations.literal: Weiguo requested establishment of a garrison commander for Yuan and Lin, recommended Vice Commander Zhao Yingkui as bold and capable; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Weiguo asked that a garrison commander be established for Yuan and Lin, and recommended Vice Commander Zhao Yingkui as a man of courage and capacity fit for the post. The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 南瑞總兵楊富謀叛，衛國廉得實，寘之法，並殲其黨，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Nanrui Garrison Commander Yang Fu plotted rebellion; Weiguo investigated and verified it, punished him by law, and destroyed his faction; the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Nanrui Garrison Commander Yang Fu plotted rebellion. Weiguo investigated until the truth was plain, punished him according to law, and wiped out his confederates. The emperor praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋改設江西總督，以命衛國。

translations.literal: Soon after the post of Governor-General of Jiangxi was created, and Weiguo was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward the office of Governor-General of Jiangxi was established, and Weiguo was appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 精忠兵及棚寇分犯新昌、上高，衛國遣諸將佟國棟、趙登舉、張射光赴援，大破賊，斬其渠左宗榜。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's troops and the Shed Bandits separately invaded Xinchang and Shanggao; Weiguo dispatched Generals Tong Guodong, Zhao Dengju, and Zhang Sheguang to reinforce; they heavily defeated the rebels and beheaded their leader Zuo Zongbang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's soldiers and the Shed Bandits struck separately at Xinchang and Shanggao. Weiguo sent Generals Tong Guodong, Zhao Dengju, and Zhang Sheguang to their aid and broke the enemy utterly, slaying their chieftain Zuo Zongbang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與希爾根等招降泰和、龍泉、永新、廬陵諸縣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, together with Xiergen and others, he induced the surrender of Taihe, Longquan, Yongxin, Luling, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he joined Xiergen and others in accepting the surrender of Taihe, Longquan, Yongxin, Luling, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 參贊桑額自上高克新昌，被檄引去；

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Sang'e took Xinchang from Shanggao, but was recalled by dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Sang'e, having advanced from Shanggao to take Xinchang, was recalled by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 寇抵隙復入，城並陷，遣其徒遏廣信糧道。

translations.literal: The rebels seized the opening and re-entered; the cities all fell, and they sent their followers to block Guangxin's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped back through the breach; the cities fell together, and they sent their bands to choke Guangxin's grain road.

sentences.zh: 衛國請督兵進剿，大將軍簡親王喇布駐師南昌，疏留之。

translations.literal: Weiguo requested to lead troops in suppression; Grand General Prince Jian Labu was stationed at Nanchang and memorialized to retain Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Weiguo asked leave to lead the army in person against the rebels, but Grand General Prince Jian Labu, encamped at Nanchang, memorialized that Weiguo be kept there.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遣諸將吳友明逐寇瑞州，复上高、新昌。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he dispatched General Wu Youming to drive the rebels from Ruizhou and recovered Shanggao and Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he sent General Wu Youming to hunt the rebels out of Ruizhou and recovered Shanggao and Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 復遣援靖安，諸將許盛、楊以鬆克泰和、定南。

translations.literal: He again sent reinforcements to Jing'an; Generals Xu Sheng and Yang Yisong took Taihe and Dingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent aid again to Jing'an, and Generals Xu Sheng and Yang Yisong recovered Taihe and Dingnan.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以土寇楊玉泰竊據宜黃、樂安、崇仁山谷中，發兵討之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, because the local bandit Yang Yutai had seized the mountain valleys of Yihuang, Le'an, and Chongren, he sent troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, learning that the local bandit Yang Yutai had seized the mountain fastnesses of Yihuang, Le'an, and Chongren, he dispatched troops to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 崇仁寇蔡仕伯、宜黃寇沈鳳祥等出降。

translations.literal: The Chongren bandit Cai Shibo, the Yihuang bandit Shen Fengxiang, and others came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Shibo of Chongren, Shen Fengxiang of Yihuang, and others came forward to surrender.

sentences.zh: 破賊於大嶺，克樂安，玉泰亦降。
