translations.literal: He defeated the rebels at Dal Ling, took Le'an, and Yutai also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the rebels on Dal Ridge, took Le'an, and Yutai surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 湖南平江及銅鼓營寇起，衛國留提督趙賴守樂安，移兵入湖南，簡親王檄發衛國標下兵悉赴樂安。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Pingjiang, Hunan, and at Tonggu Camp; Weiguo left Provincial Commander Zhao Lai to guard Le'an and moved troops into Hunan; Prince Jian issued an order that all troops under Weiguo's command should proceed to Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion flared in Pingjiang in Hunan and at Tonggu Camp. Weiguo left Provincial Commander Zhao Lai to hold Le'an and marched into Hunan, but Prince Jian ordered by dispatch that every soldier under Weiguo's banner be sent to Le'an.

sentences.zh: 衛國疏聞，且言省城駐滿洲兵不過二百，慮不足守禦，乞賜罷斥，上嚴旨詰簡親王，並諭此後徵發當諮衛國。

translations.literal: Weiguo memorialized, saying moreover that Manchu troops stationed in the provincial capital numbered no more than two hundred and he feared they were insufficient for defense; he begged to be dismissed; the emperor issued a stern edict questioning Prince Jian and decreed that hereafter levies should be consulted with Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Weiguo memorialized the throne, adding that no more than two hundred Manchu troops remained in the provincial capital—far too few, he feared, to hold the city—and begged to be dismissed from office. The emperor answered with a stern edict rebuking Prince Jian and commanded that hereafter all requisitions be taken up with Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 衛國遣兵徇建昌，定瀘溪，自將出芳塘，別遣諸將出黃岡口，遂克銅鼓營。

translations.literal: Weiguo sent troops through Jianchang and pacified Luxi; he personally led forces out from Fangtang and separately dispatched generals out from Huanggang Pass, and thus took Tonggu Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Weiguo sent columns through Jianchang and settled Luxi. He himself led the army out by Fangtang while other generals marched from Huanggang Pass, and together they took Tonggu Camp.

sentences.zh: 平江乃定。

translations.literal: Pingjiang was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was Pingjiang brought to order.

sentences.zh: 未幾，精忠將韓大任侵寧都，時簡親王出駐吉安，衛國請與會師合剿，上命綠營兵聽便宜調遣。

translations.literal: Before long, Jingzhong's general Han Daren invaded Ningdu; at the time Prince Jian was stationed at Ji'an; Weiguo requested a joint campaign; the emperor ordered Green Standard troops to be disposed at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jingzhong's general Han Daren pressed Ningdu. Prince Jian was then encamped at Ji'an, and Weiguo asked to join forces in a combined suppression. The emperor ordered that the Green Standard army be disposed at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 十七年，巡撫佟國正遣將破大任。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Governor Tong Guozheng dispatched generals and defeated Daren.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Governor Tong Guozheng sent generals against Han Daren and broke him.

sentences.zh: 精忠將郭應輔等分屯萬安、泰和諸縣，衛國督兵進擊，斬四萬餘，降者亦四萬六千有奇。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's generals Guo Yingfu and others were garrisoned separately in Wan'an, Taihe, and other counties; Weiguo led troops in attack, beheading more than forty thousand, and those who surrendered numbered also more than forty-six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's generals Guo Yingfu and others held Wan'an, Taihe, and neighboring counties in separate camps. Weiguo led the attack in person, slaying more than forty thousand men; those who surrendered numbered forty-six thousand odd besides.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂犯永興，薄吉安，上命衛國守銅鼓營。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui invaded Yongxing and approached Ji'an; the emperor ordered Weiguo to guard Tonggu Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui struck at Yongxing and drew near Ji'an, and the emperor ordered Weiguo to hold Tonggu Camp.

sentences.zh: 三桂既死，其將據岳州、長沙，師圍之未下。

translations.literal: After Sangui died, his generals held Yuezhou and Changsha; imperial forces besieged them but could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui was dead, his generals still held Yuezhou and Changsha, and though the imperial armies besieged them, the cities would not fall.

sentences.zh: 衛國請自銅鼓營督兵援剿，上嘉許，並授以方略。

translations.literal: Weiguo requested to lead troops from Tonggu Camp to reinforce suppression; the emperor praised and approved, and granted him strategic plans.
translations.idiomatic: Weiguo asked to lead the army from Tonggu Camp to their relief. The emperor praised his offer, approved it, and entrusted him with the plan of campaign.

sentences.zh: 未幾，岳州、長沙皆下。

translations.literal: Before long, Yuezhou and Changsha both fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both Yuezhou and Changsha were taken.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命會大將軍安親王岳樂謀進取，遂合軍出衡州、寶慶，破賊紫陽河、雙井鋪，克武岡。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was ordered to join Grand General Prince An Yuele in planning the advance; then combined forces marched out from Hengzhou and Baqing, defeated rebels at Ziyang River and Shuangjing Post, and took Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was ordered to confer with Grand General Prince An Yuele on the advance. The combined armies then marched out through Hengzhou and Baqing, routed the rebels at Ziyang River and Shuangjing Post, and captured Wugang.

sentences.zh: 給事中李宗孔劾衛國為總督不治事，失民心，廷議奪官，上寬之。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Li Zongkong impeached Weiguo for, as governor-general, not governing affairs and losing popular support; court deliberation recommended stripping him of office; the emperor showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Li Zongkong impeached Weiguo, charging that as governor-general he neglected his duties and had lost the people's hearts. The court recommended that he be stripped of rank, but the emperor showed him mercy.

sentences.zh: 十九年，破鴨婆、黃茅諸隘，攻靖州。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he broke through the passes at Yapo and Huangmao and attacked Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he forced the passes at Yapo and Huangmao and pressed the attack on Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 與都統穆佔會師逐吳世璠將吳應麟等，克沅州。

translations.literal: He joined forces with Commander-in-chief Muzhan to pursue Wu Shifan's generals Wu Yinglin and others and took Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He united with Commander-in-chief Muzhan to drive Wu Shifan's generals Wu Yinglin and the rest, and took Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 進薄鎮遠，力戰奪石港口，抵大岩門。

translations.literal: He advanced to press Zhenyuan, fought fiercely to seize Shipu Pass, and reached Dayan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on toward Zhenyuan, he fought fiercely, wrested Shipu Pass from the enemy, and came up to Dayan Gate.

sentences.zh: 世璠將張足法悉眾迎戰，衛國親督兵奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Shifan's general Zhang Zufa brought all his forces to meet in battle; Weiguo personally led troops in fierce assault and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan's general Zhang Zufa marched out with his whole host to give battle. Weiguo himself led the charge and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 足法夜遁，逐之至油閘關而還，遂克鎮遠。

translations.literal: Zufa fled by night; pursued him to Youzha Pass and returned, then took Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zufa fled under cover of night. Weiguo pursued him to Youzha Pass and then turned back, and Zhenyuan fell.

sentences.zh: 貴州既定，大將軍貝子彰泰下雲南，留衛國守貴陽。

translations.literal: Once Guizhou was settled, Grand General Prince Beile Zhangtai descended on Yunnan, leaving Weiguo to guard Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou was settled, Grand General Prince Beile Zhangtai marched down upon Yunnan and left Weiguo to hold Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，雲南平，命還任。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Yunnan was pacified; he was ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, with Yunnan pacified, he was ordered back to his former command.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Governor-General of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Governor-General of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 衛國初自湖南入貴州，蔡毓榮以不聽調度論劾。

translations.literal: When Weiguo first entered Guizhou from Hunan, Cai Yurong impeached him on grounds of not obeying orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiguo first crossed from Hunan into Guizhou, Cai Yurong impeached him for refusing to accept command.

sentences.zh: 事平，下廷議，上右衛國譴毓榮。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, the matter was referred to court deliberation; the emperor sided with Weiguo and censured Yurong.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign ended the matter went before the court, and the emperor upheld Weiguo and rebuked Yurong.

sentences.zh: 御史蔣伊又論衛國縱兵俘掠，江西總督於成龍為疏辯。

translations.literal: Censor Jiang Yi again impeached Weiguo for allowing troops to capture and plunder; Jiangxi Governor-General Yu Chenglong memorialized in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jiang Yi again accused Weiguo of letting his soldiers take captives and plunder at will, but Jiangxi Governor-General Yu Chenglong memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 衛國朝京師，瀕行，諭曰：「爾在外二十餘年，民情宜悉知。

translations.literal: Weiguo came to the capital; on the eve of departure, the emperor instructed: 'You have been abroad more than twenty years—you should know the people's sentiments well.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiguo came to court and, on the eve of his return, was granted audience, the emperor told him: 'You have served in the provinces more than twenty years, and ought to know the temper of the people by now.

sentences.zh: 前此方用兵，不免擾民。

translations.literal: Previously this region was at war, and disturbance of the people could not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the land was torn by war, and some harm to the common folk could not be helped.

sentences.zh: 今天下承平，當思休養，興革利病，務在實行。

translations.literal: Now the empire enjoys peace—think on rest and recovery, institute reforms and remove abuses, and see that they are truly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is at peace, you must think of letting the people breathe, of reforming what harms them and removing what oppresses them—and you must see that such things are truly done.

sentences.zh: 朕知爾有勞，毋畏人言，勉圖後效。」

translations.literal: I know your labors; do not fear men's words—strive for merit hereafter.'
translations.idiomatic: I know the weight of your service. Do not fear what men may say, but strive hereafter to prove your worth.'

sentences.zh: 月餘，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: More than a month later, he died; funeral rites were granted.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a month later he died, and the court granted him the rites of funeral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 佟國正，佟佳氏，漢軍正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Tong Guozheng, of the Tong clan, a Han bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guozheng, of the Tongjia clan, was a Han bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 自拔貢生授江南無為知州，累遷安徽按察使。

translations.literal: From a selected tribute student he was appointed Magistrate of Wuwei in Jiangnan; he rose to Regional Inspector of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from the ranks of selected tribute students, he was first made Magistrate of Wuwei in Jiangnan and rose by degrees to Regional Inspector of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，遷江西布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he was transferred to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he was transferred to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 衛國改總督，白色純代為巡撫。

translations.literal: When Weiguo was made governor-general, Bai Sechun replaced him as governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiguo was promoted to governor-general, Bai Sechun took his place as governor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，色純卒，大將軍安親王岳樂奏國正得民心，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Sechun died; Grand General Prince An Yuele memorialized that Guozheng had won popular support; he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Sechun died. Grand General Prince An Yuele memorialized that Guozheng had won the people's hearts, and he was elevated to governor.

sentences.zh: 十五年，命出駐贛州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was ordered to take field station at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was ordered to take up field command at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 叛將嚴自明等偪南康，國正遣許盛等赴援，破賊庫鎮鋪，破其壘十七，逐北七十餘裡。

translations.literal: Rebel general Yan Ziming and others pressed Nankang; Guozheng sent Xu Sheng and others to reinforce; they broke the rebels at Kuzhen Post, destroyed seventeen of their camps, and drove them north more than seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Yan Ziming and his fellows pressed upon Nankang. Guozheng sent Xu Sheng and others to their relief; they smashed the enemy at Kuzhen Post, destroyed seventeen stockades, and chased them north for more than seventy li.

sentences.zh: 自明等走南安，又遣別將黃士標、王割耳等犯信豐，國正遣楊以鬆及諸將周球等分三道擊之，士標等走南雄。

translations.literal: Ziming and others fled to Nan'an; they again sent separate generals Huang Shibiao, Wang Ge'er, and others to invade Xinfeng; Guozheng sent Yang Yisong and Generals Zhou Qiu and others in three columns to strike them; Shibiao and others fled toward Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming and the rest fled toward Nan'an, then sent other commanders—Huang Shibiao, Wang Ge'er, and the like—to strike at Xinfeng. Guozheng dispatched Yang Yisong together with Zhou Qiu and other generals in three columns against them, and Shibiao and his men retreated toward Nanxiong.

sentences.zh: 盛進克上猶，球進克龍泉。

translations.literal: Sheng advanced and took Shangyou; Qiu advanced and took Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sheng pressed forward and recovered Shangyou; Zhou Qiu pressed forward and recovered Longquan.

sentences.zh: 國正聞師定漳州，遣球及諸將劉體君等出間道援剿。

translations.literal: Guozheng heard that forces had pacified Zhangzhou; he dispatched Qiu and Generals Liu Tijun and others by secret routes to reinforce suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozheng learned that the army had settled Zhangzhou, he sent Zhou Qiu with Liu Tijun and other generals by hidden routes to join the suppression.

sentences.zh: 十六年，破賊五里排，會裡、瑞金、崇義以次下。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he defeated rebels at Wulipai; Huili, Ruijin, Chongyi, and others fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he broke the rebels at Wulipai, and Huili, Ruijin, Chongyi, and other places fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 韓大任自寧都敗竄萬安，國正遣兵四出斷道，並絕糧運；

translations.literal: Han Daren fled in defeat from Ningdu to Wan'an; Guozheng sent troops out in four directions to cut routes and also sever grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren, defeated at Ningdu, fled toward Wan'an. Guozheng sent troops out on four sides to cut his paths and choke off his grain supply.

sentences.zh: 令以鬆等追擊，戰鸕鶿寨，戰老虎洞，屢敗之。

translations.literal: He ordered Yisong and others to pursue; they fought at Luzici Stronghold and Laohu Cave and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Yisong and the rest to pursue, fighting them at Luzici Stronghold and again at Laohu Cave, and defeated them again and again.

sentences.zh: 大任走汀州，降。

translations.literal: Daren fled to Tingzhou and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Daren fled on to Tingzhou and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 江西平。

translations.literal: Jiangxi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi was at last pacified.

sentences.zh: 敘功，累進兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: For recorded merit he was successively advanced to the additional title of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were reckoned, he was repeatedly promoted until he bore the additional rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十八年，左副都御史楊雍建疏論國正蒞任數載，治績無聞。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Yongjian memorialized that Guozheng had held office several years with no recorded achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Yongjian memorialized that Guozheng had governed several years without any notable achievement to his name.

sentences.zh: 京察循例自陳，降二級調用。

translations.literal: In the capital evaluation, following routine self-report, he was demoted two ranks and reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital evaluation he made the customary self-report and was demoted two ranks and transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 周有德，字彝初，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Zhou Youde, courtesy name Yichu, a Han bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Youde, styled Yichu, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，自貢生授弘文院編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, from tribute student he was appointed Compiler of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi he entered service from the tribute students as Compiler of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 五年，從英親王阿濟格討叛將薑瓖，還，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Prince Ying Ajige to suppress rebel general Jiang Xiang; on returning he was transferred to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Prince Ying Ajige against the rebel general Jiang Xiang, and on his return was made a Reader.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，遷國史院侍讀學士，尋擢弘文院學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting of the Historiographical Institute; soon he was promoted to Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting of the Historiographical Institute, and soon afterward was elevated to Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二年，授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 三年，以獲逃人加工部侍郎銜。

translations.literal: In the third year, for capturing runaway serfs, he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, for apprehending fugitive bondservants, he was granted the additional rank of Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請寬登、萊、青三府海禁，俾居民得捕魚資生；

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized requesting relaxation of maritime prohibitions in Deng, Lai, and Qing prefectures so residents could fish for their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he memorialized to loosen the maritime prohibitions in Deng, Lai, and Qing, that the coastal people might go down to the sea and live by fishing.

sentences.zh: 請以歷城明季籓府地視民田科賦；

translations.literal: He requested that former Ming princely estates in Licheng be treated as civilian land for taxation.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the princely estates of the late Ming at Licheng be taxed as ordinary farmland.

sentences.zh: 請復孤貧口糧；

translations.literal: He requested restoration of grain rations for orphans and the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that grain rations for orphans and the utterly poor be restored.

sentences.zh: 請以德州駐防兵舊給民地五百餘頃仍還之民，駐防兵視陝西、浙江例支月糧；

translations.literal: He requested that more than five hundred qing of civilian land formerly granted to garrison troops at Dezhou be returned to the people, with garrison troops receiving monthly rations per the precedent of Shaanxi and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the more than five hundred qing of land once given the garrison at Dezhou be returned to the people, and that the garrison be paid monthly rations according to the precedent of Shaanxi and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 請蠲逋賦六十餘萬，暨察出逃亡荒蕪虛增田額戶口凡四十萬有奇，悉予免除。

translations.literal: He requested remission of more than six hundred thousand in tax arrears, and that more than four hundred thousand in inflated land quotas and registered households uncovered through investigation of flight, wasteland, and false increases all be entirely exempted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that overdue taxes totaling more than six hundred thousand be remitted, and that the more than four hundred thousand inflated land quotas and registered households uncovered among the fugitive, the abandoned, and the falsely added be wholly forgiven.

sentences.zh: 四年，濟南、兗州、東昌、青州四府旱災，請加賑恤；

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jinan, Yanzhou, Dongchang, and Qingzhou four prefectures suffered drought disaster; he requested additional relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year drought struck the four prefectures of Jinan, Yanzhou, Dongchang, and Qingzhou, and he memorialized for added relief.

sentences.zh: 登州、萊州二府歉收，請免本年額賦；

translations.literal: Dengzhou and Laizhou two prefectures had poor harvests; he requested exemption of this year's quota taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhou and Laizhou had lean harvests, and he asked that the year's assessed taxes be remitted.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All of these requests were referred to the ministries for deliberation and approved for implementation.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 七年，上遣都統特錦等會勘廣東沿海邊界，設兵防汛，俾民復業。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor dispatched the banner general Tejin and others to jointly survey the Guangdong coastal border, station troops against floods, and enable the people to resume their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor sent the banner general Tejin and others to survey the Guangdong coast, garrison troops against flooding, and allow the people to return to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 有德疏言：「界外民苦失業，聞許仍歸舊地，踴躍歡呼。

translations.literal: Youde memorialized, saying: "The people beyond the border suffered bitterly from losing their occupations; hearing that they were permitted to return to their old lands, they leaped and shouted for joy.
translations.idiomatic: Youde memorialized: "The people beyond the border had suffered terribly from displacement; when they heard they would be allowed back to their old lands, they leaped and shouted for joy.

sentences.zh: 第海濱遼闊，使待勘界既明，始議安插，尚需時日，窮民迫不及待。

translations.literal: But the seacoast is vast and remote; if they must wait until the border survey is complete before resettlement is discussed, that will still require time, and the destitute cannot wait.
translations.idiomatic: But the coast is vast and far-flung; if they must wait until the survey is finished and resettlement can be discussed, many days will still pass, and the poorest cannot wait that long.

sentences.zh: 請令州縣官按遷戶版籍給還故業。」

translations.literal: I request that district and county officials, according to the registers of relocated households, return their former properties."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that district and county magistrates, using the registers of relocated households, restore their former holdings at once.

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: The memorial received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 是冬，遭父喪，平南王尚可喜疏言沿海兵民，方賴經營安輯，請命在任守制。

translations.literal: That winter he suffered his father's death. The Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, memorialized that coastal troops and civilians relied on Youde's management for peace and requested that he be permitted to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: That winter his father died. Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi memorialized that coastal soldiers and civilians still depended on Youde's stewardship for order, and asked that he be allowed to observe mourning without leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 凡三年而事定。

translations.literal: In all, after three years the affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Three years passed before the business was fully settled.

sentences.zh: 九年，疏請還京師治喪，許之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he memorialized requesting return to the capital to observe mourning; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he memorialized to return to the capital and mourn properly; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十年，旱，求言，編修陳志紀疏言：「上憂勤惕厲，而嘗為督撫諸大臣方營第宅，蓄倡優，近在輦轂下，不守法度，何以責遠方大吏廉節？」

translations.literal: In the tenth year there was drought and the emperor solicited advice. Compiler Chen Zhiji memorialized, saying: "The emperor is vigilant and diligent in his cares, yet former governors and grand coordinators are building mansions and keeping actors and singers right under the capital's eyes, not observing the law — how can one demand probity from distant grand officials?"
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year drought struck and the throne called for counsel. Compiler Chen Zhiji wrote: "Your Majesty toils in vigilance and restraint, yet former governors and grand coordinators are erecting mansions and keeping actors and singers within sight of the capital, heedless of the law — how then can distant grand officials be held to probity?

sentences.zh: 上命指實，覆疏舉郎廷佐、張長庚、苗澄，祖澤溥、張朝璘、許世昌並及有德，下部嚴察，有德坐居喪營造，又於志紀覆疏未入時，囑託毋及其名，奪官，追繳誥命。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered specific accusations. In a follow-up memorial Chen named Lang Tingzuo, Zhang Changgeng, Miao Cheng, Zu Zepu, Zhang Chaolin, Xu Shichang, and also Youde. The case was referred to the ministries for strict investigation. Youde was convicted of building during mourning; moreover, before Chen's follow-up memorial had been submitted, he had petitioned that his name not be included. He was dismissed from office and ordered to surrender his patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chen to name names. In a follow-up memorial he cited Lang Tingzuo, Zhang Changgeng, Miao Cheng, Zu Zepu, Zhang Chaolin, Xu Shichang, and Youde as well; the case went to the ministries for strict inquiry. Youde was found guilty of undertaking construction while in mourning and, worse, of having lobbied to keep his name out before Chen's second memorial reached the throne. He was stripped of office and made to return his patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，十三年，起授四川總督。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled. In the thirteenth year Youde was recalled and appointed Governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rose in rebellion, Youde was recalled in the thirteenth year and made governor of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三桂將吳之茂、彭時亨等犯廣元，有德與副都統科爾寬分道擊敗之，陣斬裨將徐應昌等。

translations.literal: Sangui's generals Wu Zhimao, Peng Shiheng, and others invaded Guangyuan. Youde and Vice Banner Commander Ke'erkuo split forces and defeated them, killing assistant generals Xu Yingchang and others in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's generals Wu Zhimao and Peng Shiheng attacked Guangyuan. Youde and Vice Banner Commander Ke'erkuo divided their forces, routed them, and killed the assistant general Xu Yingchang and others on the field.

sentences.zh: 上命經略尚書莫洛自陝西入四川，敕有德與巡撫張德地固守廣元諸路，並督軍餉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Pacification Minister Mo Luo to enter Sichuan from Shaanxi and instructed Youde and Governor Zhang Dedi to hold firm the Guangyuan routes and supervise military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Pacification Minister Mo Luo to advance into Sichuan from Shaanxi and charged Youde and Governor Zhang Dedi to hold the Guangyuan lines and oversee army supplies.

sentences.zh: 三桂將何德成等自昭化攻二郎關，謀奪我師儲峙，有德遣兵擊德成，走還昭化，复犯廣元；

translations.literal: Sangui's generals He Decheng and others attacked Erlang Pass from Zhaohua, planning to seize our army's stored supplies. Youde sent troops against Decheng, who fled back to Zhaohua and again invaded Guangyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's general He Decheng and others struck Erlang Pass from Zhaohua, aiming to seize our stored provisions. Youde sent troops against Decheng, who fell back to Zhaohua and then struck at Guangyuan again;

sentences.zh: 有德與科爾寬等復擊敗之，逐北三十餘裡。

translations.literal: Youde with Ke'erkuo and others again defeated them and drove them north more than thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Youde and Ke'erkuo defeated them once more and pursued them north for more than thirty li.

sentences.zh: 時亨屯七盤、朝天諸關，劫略陽糧艘，廣元餉不給。

translations.literal: Shiheng stationed at Qipan, Chaotian, and other passes, plundering Yang grain boats; Guangyuan's provisions were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng held Qipan, Chaotian, and the other passes, looting grain boats on the Yang route, so that Guangyuan's supplies ran dry.

sentences.zh: 寇窺陽平，將軍席卜臣屯蟠龍山為所劫，斷我師餉道，上命有德固守陽平諸路。

translations.literal: Bandits watched Yangping. General Xibuchen, garrisoned at Panlong Mountain, was robbed by them, cutting our army's supply route. The emperor ordered Youde to hold firm the Yangping routes.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces threatened Yangping. General Xibuchen, encamped on Panlong Mountain, was raided and his supply line severed. The emperor ordered Youde to secure the Yangping routes.

sentences.zh: 王輔臣叛，十四年，上命大將軍貝​​勒董額討之，以有德參贊軍務，命督諸軍協擊。

translations.literal: Wang Fuchen rebelled. In the fourteenth year the emperor ordered Grand General Prince-le Beile Dong'e to suppress him, with Youde as military adviser and ordered to direct all armies in coordinated attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchen turned rebel. In the fourteenth year the emperor sent Grand General Prince-le Beile Dong'e against him, with Youde as adviser on military affairs and orders to coordinate the joint assault.

sentences.zh: 董額克秦州，有德乞還誥命，吏部持非例，上特許之。

translations.literal: Dong'e captured Qinzhou. Youde begged for the return of his patent of nobility. The Board of Civil Officials objected as irregular; the emperor specially permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'e took Qinzhou. Youde petitioned to have his patent of nobility restored. The Board of Civil Officials held that this was not customary, but the emperor made an exception and granted it.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從大將軍大學士圖海攻平涼，輔臣降。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Grand General and Grand Secretary Tu Hai in attacking Pingliang; Fuchen surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he marched with Grand General and Grand Secretary Tu Hai against Pingliang, and Fuchen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 圖海疏令有德還駐西安。

translations.literal: Tu Hai memorialized ordering Youde to return and garrison at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai memorialized that Youde should withdraw and take up garrison duty at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 之茂等尚駐秦嶺，十七年，與副都統覺和託督兵擊之，降其裨將王世祜等。

translations.literal: Zhimao and others still held the Qinling. In the seventeenth year, with Vice Banner Commander Jioheto he directed troops against them and accepted the surrender of assistant generals Wang Shihu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhimao and his men still held the Qinling. In the seventeenth year Youde and Vice Banner Commander Jioheto led troops against them and received the surrender of assistant generals such as Wang Shihu.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 師克漢中，上諭責「有德、德地等前駐廣元督餉遲誤，致數年來逆賊逋誅，兵民苦累。

translations.literal: When the army captured Hanzhong, the emperor rebuked them, saying: "Youde, Dedi, and others previously garrisoned at Guangyuan supervising provisions with delays, causing the rebels to escape punishment for years and troops and civilians to suffer.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanzhong fell, the emperor rebuked them: "Youde, Dedi, and the rest once garrisoned Guangyuan and delayed the provisioning of the army, so that for years the rebels escaped punishment and soldiers and civilians bore the cost.

sentences.zh: 今大兵前進，督撫諸臣有誤餉運，以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: Now the great army advances; if governors and grand coordinators err in supply transport, military law will be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the main force is advancing, any governor or grand coordinator who mishandles supply transport will be dealt with under military law."

sentences.zh: 王大臣議師自湖廣進徵雲、貴，綠旗兵當有統帥，以湖廣總督蔡毓榮及有德名上，上以命毓榮，令有德受節制。

translations.literal: Princes and ministers deliberated that the army should advance from Huguang to campaign in Yunnan and Guizhou; the Green Standard troops needed a commander-in-chief. They submitted the names of Huguang Governor Cai Yurong and Youde. The emperor appointed Yurong and ordered Youde to accept his command.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and ministers agreed that the expedition into Yunnan and Guizhou should advance from Huguang and that the Green Standard forces required a supreme commander. They put forward Huguang Governor Cai Yurong and Youde; the emperor named Yurong and placed Youde under his orders.

sentences.zh: 有德尋疾作，留駐常德。

translations.literal: Youde soon fell ill and remained garrisoned at Changde.
translations.idiomatic: Youde soon fell ill and stayed behind at Changde.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 張德地，初名劉格，漢軍鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Zhang Dedi, original name Liu Ge, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dedi, originally named Liu Ge, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 初以通曉國書，在戶部學習。

translations.literal: Initially, for mastery of the national script, he studied in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the Ministry of Revenue as a trainee because of his command of Manchu.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，授宗人府主事，累遷戶部督捕理事官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he was appointed registrar of the Imperial Clan Court and was promoted in successive steps to commissioner for bandit suppression in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he was made a registrar in the Imperial Clan Court and rose step by step to commissioner for bandit suppression in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，擢順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he was promoted to intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he was promoted to intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年，授四川巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed governor of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「四川自張獻忠亂後，地曠人稀，請招民承墾。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Since Zhang Xianzhong's rebellion, Sichuan's land is vast and its people sparse; I request that settlers be recruited to reclaim the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Since the devastation of Zhang Xianzhong's rebellion, Sichuan has lain largely empty; I ask that settlers be recruited to reopen the land.

sentences.zh: 文武吏招民百戶、墾田十頃以上，予遷轉。」

translations.literal: Civil and military officials who recruit one hundred households and reclaim more than ten qing of land shall receive promotion and transfer."
translations.idiomatic: Any civil or military officer who brings in a hundred households and reclaims more than ten qing of land should be rewarded with promotion.

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries and approved.

sentences.zh: 累加工部尚書銜。

translations.literal: He was successively given the additional title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly granted the additional rank of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十年，武生劉琯等訐德地主武鄉試得賄鬻武舉，遣副都御史阿範等按治，德地坐斬，命免死奪官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the military licentiate Liu Guan and others accused Dedi of taking bribes in the military provincial examination to sell military juren titles. Vice Censor-in-Chief A Fan and others were dispatched to investigate. Dedi was sentenced to decapitation; the emperor ordered that he be spared death but stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the military licentiate Liu Guan and others charged that Dedi had taken bribes in the military provincial examination to sell juren degrees. Vice Censor-in-Chief A Fan was sent to investigate. Dedi was sentenced to death; the emperor commuted the sentence to dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 德地叩閽稱枉，下部覆議，以事無據，复官。

translations.literal: Dedi petitioned at the Gate claiming injustice. The ministries reconsidered and, finding no evidence, restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Dedi beat the Gate drum protesting his innocence. The ministries reviewed the case, found no proof, and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 十三年，复授四川巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was again appointed Governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was again made governor of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時亨犯廣元，德地與有德督兵御之。

translations.literal: When Shiheng invaded Guangyuan, Dedi with Youde directed troops to repel him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiheng attacked Guangyuan, Dedi and Youde jointly commanded the defense.

sentences.zh: 十四年，王輔臣叛，命協守西安，尋又命出駐延安。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Wang Fuchen rebelled; he was ordered to assist in defending Xi'an, and soon was also ordered to go out and garrison at Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when Wang Fuchen rebelled, he was ordered to help hold Xi'an and soon afterward to take the field at Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 廣元之役，有德劾德地棄城走，奪官。

translations.literal: In the Guangyuan campaign, Youde impeached Dedi for abandoning the city and fleeing; Dedi was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangyuan fighting, Youde impeached Dedi for abandoning the city and fleeing, and Dedi was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he died.

sentences.zh: 伊闢，字盧源，山東新城人。

translations.literal: Yi Pi, styled Luyuan, was a native of Xincheng, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Pi, styled Luyuan, came from Xincheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he took first place in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 十二年，成進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he passed the jinshi examination and became a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he passed the jinshi examination and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授御史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，巡按山西，捕長治亂民勒化龍，窮治其黨與。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, touring Shanxi as investigating censor, he captured the Changzhi rebel Le Hualong and thoroughly punished his associates.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, on an investigating tour of Shanxi, he seized the Changzhi rebel Le Hualong and rooted out his whole faction.

sentences.zh: 十六年，還，掌京畿道，擢通政司參議。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he returned, took charge of the Metropolitan circuit, and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he returned to the capital, took charge of the Metropolitan circuit, and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 累遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to president of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in successive appointments to president of the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，授雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi he was appointed Governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi he was appointed governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時吳世璠未平，師自廣西、貴州、四川分道入，闢督餉。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Shifan had not yet been pacified. Armies entered by separate routes from Guangxi, Guizhou, and Sichuan, and Pi supervised provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan was not yet subdued. Imperial columns entered from Guangxi, Guizhou, and Sichuan by separate routes, and Pi took charge of provisioning.

sentences.zh: 圍會城未下，同知劉昆不屈於三桂，為所縶，至是始脫出。

translations.literal: The siege of the provincial capital had not yet succeeded. Subprefect Liu Kun had refused to submit to Sangui, was imprisoned by him, and only now escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial capital was still under siege. Subprefect Liu Kun had refused to yield to Sangui, was taken prisoner, and had only just made his escape.

sentences.zh: 闢從諮策，昆曰：「公用人寬，降人予原職。

translations.literal: Pi sought his counsel. Kun said: "Your lordship employs men leniently and restores surrendered men to their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Pi asked his advice. Kun said: "You are lenient in your appointments and put surrendered men back in their old offices.

sentences.zh: 今安寧、晉寧、昆陽、呈貢諸縣令悉降人，昆池舟楫往來無禁。

translations.literal: Now the magistrates of Anning, Jinning, Kunyang, and Chenggong are all surrendered men, and boats on Kunming Lake come and go without restriction.
translations.idiomatic: At present the magistrates of Anning, Jinning, Kunyang, and Chenggong are all former rebels, and traffic on Kunming Lake moves without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 豈有父兄被圍而子弟不為轉輸者？」

translations.literal: How can there be fathers and elder brothers besieged while sons and younger brothers do not supply transport?"
translations.idiomatic: When fathers and elder brothers are under siege, will their sons and younger brothers not keep the supplies moving?

sentences.zh: 闢為罷諸降人，寇餉漸斷。

translations.literal: Pi accordingly dismissed all the surrendered officials, and the rebels' provisions were gradually cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Pi thereupon removed all the surrendered officials from office, and the enemy's supplies began to fail.

sentences.zh: 師久次，慮餉不繼。

translations.literal: The army lingered long and feared that provisions would not continue.
translations.idiomatic: The army had camped for a long time, and there was fear the supplies would run out.

sentences.zh: 闢疏請貴州、廣西二路協濟銀米，上以二路道險山多，轉運不便，遣戶部郎中明額禮、薩木哈詣軍酌議採買。

translations.literal: Pi memorialized requesting silver and grain from the Guizhou and Guangxi routes. The emperor said both routes have dangerous mountains and transport is inconvenient, and dispatched Revenue Ministry directors Ming'eli and Samuha to the army to discuss local purchasing.
translations.idiomatic: Pi memorialized for silver and grain from Guizhou and Guangxi. The emperor replied that both routes were mountainous and treacherous and overland transport impracticable, and sent Revenue Ministry directors Ming'eli and Samuha to the front to arrange local purchases.

sentences.zh: 軍中或議取食民間，布政使王繼文持不可，曰：「現糧支三日，昆陽、宜良寇遺糧，方具資庀役運詣軍前。

translations.literal: Some in the army discussed taking food from the people. Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Jiwen objected, saying: "Present grain will last three days. Abandoned grain left by the rebels at Kunyang and Yiliang is being organized and transported to the army front.
translations.idiomatic: Some officers proposed requisitioning food from the populace. Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Jiwen objected: "We have grain for three days on hand. Grain the rebels left at Kunyang and Yiliang is being gathered and sent forward.

sentences.zh: 兩廣隨軍餉銀十萬在曲靖，當請於總督金光祖，乞相假。

translations.literal: One hundred thousand taels of military provision silver from the Two Guangs is at Qujing; we should request Governor Jin Guangzu to lend it.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand taels of campaign funds from Guangdong and Guangxi are at Qujing; we should ask Governor Jin Guangzu to advance them.

sentences.zh: 過三日餉不繼，請正繼文軍法。」

translations.literal: If after three days provisions do not continue, I request that military law be applied to Jiwen."
translations.idiomatic: If supplies still fail after three days, I ask that I myself be punished under military law."

sentences.zh: 闢言於大將軍貝子彰泰，用其議。

translations.literal: Pi reported to Grand General Prince Zhentai and adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Pi laid the plan before Grand General Prince Zhentai, who accepted it.

sentences.zh: 不三日，銀粟皆至，民以得安，餉亦無闕。

translations.literal: Within three days silver and grain all arrived; the people were thereby kept safe and the provisions were without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: In less than three days silver and grain both arrived; the people were spared harm and the army's needs were met.

sentences.zh: 闢疏言：「雲南地處天末，當得重臣彈壓。

translations.literal: Pi memorialized, saying: "Yunnan stands at the edge of heaven and ought to have a weighty minister to hold it down.
translations.idiomatic: Pi memorialized: "Yunnan lies at the uttermost edge of the realm and requires a senior minister to keep it in hand.

sentences.zh: 元鎮以親王，明則黔國公任留守。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan a prince served as military governor; under the Ming the Duke of Qian served as resident commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan posted a prince as military governor; the Ming entrusted the Duke of Qian with the garrison.

sentences.zh: 王師計日蕩平，臣自鎮遠至雲南，途次聞士民語，僉謂大將軍貝子彰泰、內大臣額駙華善所過不擾，請特簡一人鎮守。」

translations.literal: The imperial armies will soon pacify all. Traveling from Zhenyuan to Yunnan I heard the people say unanimously that Grand General Prince Zhentai and Inner Minister and Imperial Son-in-law Huashan pass without disturbing them; I request that one man be specially selected to garrison the province."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies will soon sweep the province clean. From Zhenyuan to Yunnan I heard the same report everywhere: Grand General Prince Zhentai and Inner Minister and Imperial Son-in-law Huashan march without troubling the people. I ask that a single senior appointee be chosen to hold the province afterward.

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 闢旋病作，遺疏薦繼文自代。

translations.literal: Pi soon fell ill and in a dying memorial recommended Jiwen to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi soon fell ill and, in a final memorial, recommended Jiwen as his successor.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: He died and was granted funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 繼文，字在燕，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Jiwen, styled Zaiyan, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwen, styled Zaiyan, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 自官學生授弘文院編修，遷兵部督捕副理事官。

translations.literal: From Imperial Academy student he was appointed compiler of the Hanlin Academy and transferred to vice commissioner for bandit suppression in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from the Imperial Academy, he was made a Hanlin compiler and then transferred to vice commissioner for bandit suppression in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，考選御史，巡按陝西。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was selected as censor and toured Shaanxi as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was chosen censor and sent on an investigating tour of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初受事，即疏劾布政使黃紀、興屯道白士麟貪污不法，奪官逮治。

translations.literal: Upon taking office he immediately memorialized impeaching Provincial Administration Commissioner Huang Ji and Agricultural Reclamation Intendant Bai Shilin for corruption and illegal conduct; they were stripped of office and arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The moment he took up his post he impeached Provincial Administration Commissioner Huang Ji and Agricultural Reclamation Intendant Bai Shilin for graft and malfeasance; both were dismissed and arrested.

sentences.zh: 十四年，還京師，都察院列上繼文在官劾文武吏四十餘，督開荒田七千頃有奇，招徠流移民五千八百餘，察出虛冒錢糧七千七百有奇，實心任事，允為稱職。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he returned to the capital. The Censorate listed that in office Jiwen had impeached more than forty civil and military officials, supervised the opening of more than seven thousand qing of wasteland, recruited more than five thousand eight hundred displaced migrants, and uncovered more than seven thousand seven hundred in falsely claimed taxes and grain — he served conscientiously and was truly competent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he returned to the capital. The Censorate reported that in Shaanxi Jiwen had impeached more than forty civil and military officers, overseen the reclamation of over seven thousand qing of wasteland, brought in more than five thousand eight hundred displaced settlers, and exposed more than seven thousand seven hundred in false tax and grain claims — a record of conscientious service that fully justified his promotion.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to a directorship in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授江西饒九南道。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed intendant of the Rao-Jiunan Circuit in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made intendant of the Rao-Jiunan circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，調浙江寧紹台道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he was transferred to the Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kangxi he was transferred to the Ning-Shao-Tai circuit in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 六年，缺裁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the post was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year that post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 十三年，師討吳三桂，命以候補道從左都御史多諾等如荊州督餉，用繼文策度地建倉，分餽東西二路軍及水師。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the army campaigned against Wu Sangui, he was ordered as a candidate intendant to follow Left Censor-in-Chief Duonuo and others to Jingzhou to supervise provisions. Jiwen's plan to survey the land, build granaries, and distribute supplies to the eastern and western route armies and the navy was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, during the campaign against Wu Sangui, he was sent as a candidate intendant with Left Censor-in-Chief Duonuo and others to Jingzhou to manage supplies. His scheme to survey sites, erect granaries, and feed the eastern and western columns and the river force was put into effect.

sentences.zh: 旋授雲南布政使，從師進徵。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan and followed the army on the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan and marched with the expedition.

sentences.zh: 二十年，代闢為巡撫，佐將軍趙良棟攻克會城，雲南遂定。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he replaced Pi as governor, assisted General Zhao Liangdong in capturing the provincial capital, and Yunnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he succeeded Pi as governor, helped General Zhao Liangdong take the provincial capital, and Yunnan was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，與總督蔡毓榮疏言：「會城東南舊有金汁河，引盤龍江水入昆明池，舊存壩閘涵洞，積水溉田。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he and Governor Cai Yurong memorialized, saying: "Southeast of the provincial capital there was formerly the Jinzhi River, which drew Panlong River water into Kunming Lake. Dams, sluices, and culverts once stored water to irrigate the fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he and Governor Cai Yurong wrote: "Southeast of the capital lay the old Jinzhi River, which channeled Panlong River water into Kunming Lake through dams, sluices, and culverts to irrigate the fields.

sentences.zh: 世璠毀為壕塹，令官吏捐資修治。」

translations.literal: Shifan destroyed them as trenches; order the officials to contribute funds for repair."
translations.idiomatic: Shifan had torn them up for trenches; we ask that officials be ordered to contribute toward their restoration.

sentences.zh: 下部議，捐銀百，紀錄一次。

translations.literal: The ministries deliberated and ordered a donation of one hundred taels of silver and one recorded merit.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved the plan, with a contribution of one hundred taels of silver and one recorded merit for the memorialists.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以憂歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he returned home to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he went home to mourn a parent's death.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，复授巡撫，疏言：「黑井鹽課，三桂月增課銀二千兩，請豁除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was again appointed governor and memorialized, saying: "At Heijing the salt levy — Sangui had increased the monthly quota by two thousand taels of silver; I request that this be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was again made governor and memorialized: "At the Heijing salt works Sangui had added two thousand taels of silver to the monthly levy; I ask that this surcharge be abolished.

sentences.zh: 屯田科賦十倍於民田，重為民累，請分別改視民田起科。」

translations.literal: Military colony taxes are ten times those on civilian fields and heavily burden the people; I request that they be separately reclassified and taxed at civilian rates."
translations.idiomatic: Taxes on military colony land run ten times those on ordinary farmland and crush the people; I ask that they be reclassified and assessed like civilian holdings.

sentences.zh: 三十年，疏言：「土司奏銷遲誤，例無處分，請比照流官計俸罰米，移貯附近常平倉備荒賑。」

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he memorialized, saying: "When native chieftains delay in submitting their accounts there is no regulation for punishment; I request that, by analogy with regular officials, salary be calculated and grain fines imposed, to be stored in nearby Ever-Normal granaries for famine relief."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he wrote: "Native chieftains who delay their accounts face no penalty; I propose that, as with regular officials, fines in grain be assessed from their salaries and deposited in nearby Ever-Normal granaries for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 皆議行。

translations.literal: All were approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，討平魯魁山寇，釐定汛界，駐兵防守。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he suppressed the bandits at Lukuishan, demarcated garrison boundaries, and stationed troops to defend them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he put down the Lukuishan bandits, fixed the garrison boundaries, and posted troops to hold them.

sentences.zh: 又疏議收水西宣慰使地，改屬大定、平遠、黔西三州流官管轄，均如所請。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to annex the lands of the Shuixi Pacification Commissioner and transfer them to the jurisdiction of the regular officials of the three prefectures of Dading, Pingyuan, and Qianxi; all was granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed bringing the Shuixi Pacification Commissioner's territory under the regular administration of Dading, Pingyuan, and Qianxi; all was approved as he asked.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬，朝京師，以老病乞致仕。

translations.literal: That winter he went to the capital and, aged and ill, requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he traveled to the capital and, being old and infirm, asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 尋命修理子牙河工。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to repair the works on the Ziya River.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to oversee repairs on the Ziya River.

sentences.zh: 賜御書榜曰「煙霞耆舊」。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial inscribed plaque reading "Elder among Mist and Clouds."
translations.idiomatic: The throne bestowed an imperial plaque inscribed "Elder among Mist and Clouds."

sentences.zh: 四十年，加兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was given the additional title of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he received the additional rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he died, and funeral sacrifices were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-second year, and the court granted him the rites of funeral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子用霖，官山東布政使。

translations.literal: His son Yonglin served as Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yonglin rose to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 論曰：毓榮統綠旗兵下雲南，廉清不逮趙良棟，戰績與相亞。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Yurong commanded the Green Standard troops south into Yunnan; in integrity and austerity he did not match Zhao Liangdong, yet his battle achievements were nearly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Yurong led the Green Standard army into Yunnan. He was not Zhao Liangdong's equal in probity, but his military record stood nearly on a par.

sentences.zh: 哈佔鎮陝西，衛國定江西，有德略四川，督餉治軍，其於戡亂皆與有功。

translations.literal: Hazhan held Shaanxi, Weiguo settled Jiangxi, Youde secured Sichuan, supervising supplies and governing the army—in suppressing rebellion each had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Hazhan held Shaanxi, Weiguo pacified Jiangxi, and Youde secured Sichuan while supervising provisions and disciplining the troops; each contributed materially to putting down the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 雲南既下，撫綏安集之績，毓榮開之，繼文成之，自是西南遂底於平矣。

translations.literal: Once Yunnan had fallen, the achievement of pacification and settlement was begun by Yurong and continued by Jiwen; from then on the southwest was brought to lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan fell, the work of pacification and resettlement was begun by Yurong and carried on by Jiwen; from that point the southwest was settled for good.
